item.title: Wadephul droht Iran wegen Anschlägs-Plänen: "Wir werden reagieren"
item.description: Bundesaußenminister Johann Wadephul hat vor hybriden Angriffen des Iran in Europa gewarnt und der Führung in Teheran mit Konsequenzen gedroht. "Europa ist im Fadenkreuz Irans", sagte Wadephul bei einer Pressekonferenz mit dem portugiesischen Außenminister Paulo Rangel am Freitag in Berlin. Der Minister begrüßte zugleich ein Urteil des Hamburger Oberlandesgerichts, das am Donnerstag zwei Männer mit Verbindungen zum Iran wegen versuchter Mordanschläge auf Juden in Deutschland zu mehrjährigen Haftstrafen verurteilt hatte. Dabei kündigte Wadephul eine Reaktion der Bundesregierung an.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bundesaußenminister Johann Wadephul hat vor hybriden Angriffen des Iran in Europa gewarnt und der Führung in Teheran mit Konsequenzen gedroht. "Europa ist im Fadenkreuz Irans", sagte Wadephul bei einer Pressekonferenz mit dem portugiesischen Außenminister Paulo Rangel am Freitag in Berlin. Der Minister begrüßte zugleich ein Urteil des Hamburger Oberlandesgerichts, das am Donnerstag zwei Männer mit Verbindungen zum Iran wegen versuchter Mordanschläge auf Juden in Deutschland zu mehrjährigen Haftstrafen verurteilt hatte. Dabei kündigte Wadephul eine Reaktion der Bundesregierung an. "Wir nehmen die feindseligen Aktivitäten Irans nicht hin, die sich gegen Jüdinnen und Juden hier in Deutschland und unsere offene Gesellschaft insgesamt richten", sagte Wadephul. "Es ist gut, dass die versuchten Attentate gegen Josef Schuster und Volker Beck und die Rolle Irans hinter diesem staatlich gelenkten Terror so klar benannt wurden", betonte er mit Blick auf den Präsidenten des Zentralrats der Juden in Deutschland und den Präsidenten der Deutsch-Israelischen Gesellschaft. "Auch hier werden wir reagieren." Das Hamburger Gericht kam zu der Überzeugung, dass einer der Verurteilten vom iranischen Geheimdienst gesteuert wurde. Der dänische Staatsbürger Ali S. wurde wegen der Vorbereitung eines Attentats und schwerer Brandstiftung zu acht Jahren und sechs Monaten Haft verurteilt. Die Richter seien davon überzeugt, dass der Angeklagte vom iranischen Geheimdienst rekrutiert und in dessen Strukturen eingebunden worden sei, um unter der Leitung des Irans staatlich gesteuerte Terroranschläge in Deutschland zu verüben. Der zweite Angeklagte, ein afghanischer Staatsbürger, erhielt wegen seiner Beteiligung an den Anschlagsplänen eine Haftstrafe von vier Jahren und sechs Monaten. Wadephul verwies auch darauf, dass Großbritannien einen versuchten Anschlag auf einen militärischen Stützpunkt in Fairfield dem Iran zugeschrieben habe.

item.title: Knicks chase back-to-back banner in NBA built to stop dynasties
item.description: New York has barely stopped celebrating its first NBA title in 53 years, and the Knicks are already chasing a repeat in a league that is built to stop one.
item.dc:creator: Rory Carroll
item.content:encoded: New York has barely stopped celebrating its first NBA title in 53 years, and the Knicks are already chasing a repeat in a league that is built to stop one. The NBA has crowned a record eight different champions in the last eight seasons. Rules that make it tougher to stack a roster with superstars have turned the league into a free-for-all. The Knicks, however, have a big edge: the band is back together. New York returns its five best players, Jalen Brunson, Josh Hart, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns, along with the chemistry that carried it to the title. THE LEBRON PLOT TWIST The offseason's biggest story was where the NBA's all-time leading scorer, LeBron James, would land after splitting with the Los Angeles Lakers. The surprise winner of the sweepstakes was the Philadelphia 76ers. James admitted he would have liked to play for the Knicks, but said that door closed once they won the title. So the 41-year-old will take his talents to Philadelphia instead of the Big Apple, although he will reportedly be living part-time in New York and commuting by helicopter. There he joins Jaylen Brown, who was stunningly traded by the Celtics in the offseason, along with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe. The question is whether the pieces fit, since all five players are accustomed to having the ball in their hands. "They are like a room that has five beautiful couches in it," ESPN's Brian Windhorst told ABS-CBN News. "But you don't need five couches in a room. You need a couch and a chair, a table, a TV and a mirror, and that's going to be a challenge. Can they all fit, or do you have to put one couch up along the wall." WELCOME TO THE GARDEN James could hardly have a more dramatic debut. The four-time champion opens his Philadelphia career at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday, just after the Knicks raise their championship banner. His teams have often started slowly in his first season with them. If that happens again, Philadelphia's famously impatient fans may not wait long to let everyone know how they feel. The payoff could be historic. A title in his record-extending 24th season would make James the first player to win championships with four different teams. EVERYONE ELSE WANTS IN The rest of the league has its own plans when the 2026-27 season tips off on Tuesday: Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs want revenge after a bitter Finals loss. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Oklahoma City Thunder are going for a second title in three years. Stephen Curry leads a Golden State Warriors team trying to revive its title hopes.

item.title: Hohe Kerosinpreise - Eurowings streicht Flüge und prüft Kurzarbeit
item.description: Die Lufthansa-Tochter Eurowings erwägt Kurzarbeit im Winter und streicht Flüge, um die Kostenbelastungen wegen des teuren Kerosins abzupuffern. "Wir prüfen aktuell, ob die Voraussetzungen für temporäre Kurzarbeit im deutschen Flugbetrieb im Winter gegeben sind", erklärte die Airline am Freitag. Zuerst hatte der "Spiegel" darüber berichtet. Die Fluggesellschaft führt bereits Gespräche mit der Bundesagentur für Arbeit, wie aus einem Schreiben an die Belegschaft hervorgeht, das auch der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters vorlag. Offen blieb, wie viele Beschäftigte betroffen sind.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) -Tochter Eurowings erwägt Kurzarbeit im Winter und streicht Flüge, um die Kostenbelastungen wegen des teuren Kerosins abzupuffern. "Wir prüfen aktuell, ob die Voraussetzungen für temporäre Kurzarbeit im deutschen Flugbetrieb im Winter gegeben sind", erklärte die Airline am Freitag. Zuerst hatte der "Spiegel" darüber berichtet. Die Fluggesellschaft führt bereits Gespräche mit der Bundesagentur für Arbeit, wie aus einem Schreiben an die Belegschaft hervorgeht, das auch der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters vorlag. Offen blieb, wie viele Beschäftigte betroffen sind. Hohe Kerosinpreise infolge des Iran-Kriegs setzen Airlines weltweit unter Druck. Die Lufthansa-Gruppe erwartet in diesem Jahr wegen des gestiegenen Kerosinpreises eine höhere Belastung als bisher, hatte Konzernchef [USN:L8N45L0AC TEXT:"Carsten Spohr"] jüngst erklärt. "Allein für Eurowings bedeutet das im laufenden Jahr fast 250 Millionen Euro mehr Kerosinkosten als geplant – eine gewaltige Summe", heißt es in dem Brief. Als Reaktion darauf kürze Eurowings das Winterangebot bereits in einem ersten Schritt um rund fünf Prozent. Die Verbindungen von Köln/Bonn und Stuttgart nach Dubai entfallen. Zudem sei die interne Weihnachtsfeier abgesagt worden und Eurowings solle etwa in der Verwaltung bis Ende 2028 mit rund 100 Stellen weniger auskommen. Eurowings steht nach Einschätzung der Geschäftsführung zwar besser da als andere Wettbewerber, ist aber nicht immun gegen Krisen. "Trotz weiterhin gut gebuchter Flüge gilt es, eine Lücke zwischen Einnahmen und Ausgaben zu schließen, die in den jetzt bevorstehenden, traditionell schwierigen Wintermonaten absehbar größer wird", schreibt das Management in dem Brief. "Erschwerend kommt hinzu, dass sich bei den rekordhohen Kerosinpreisen auch für 2027 keine Entlastung abzeichnet." Die gesamte Luftfahrtbranche versucht gegenzusteuern. So kündigte jüngst auch der Berliner Hauptstadtflughafen BER ein [USN:L8N45Y0O7 TEXT:"Sparprogramm"] an und will seine Kosten senken sowie bestimmte Investitionen verschieben.

item.title: US-Firmen fahren Produktion im September hoch
item.description: Die US-Unternehmen haben ihre Produktion im September stärker gesteigert als erwartet. Die Fertigung von Industrie, Versorgern und Bergbau legte um 0,7 Prozent zu, wie die US-Notenbank Federal Reserve (Fed) am Freitag mitteilte. Von der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters befragte Experten hatten nur mit einem Zuwachs von 0,4 Prozent gerechnet.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die US-Unternehmen haben ihre Produktion im September stärker gesteigert als erwartet. Die Fertigung von Industrie, Versorgern und Bergbau legte um 0,7 Prozent zu, wie die US-Notenbank Federal Reserve (Fed) am Freitag mitteilte. Von der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters befragte Experten hatten nur mit einem Zuwachs von 0,4 Prozent gerechnet. Im Vormonat August hatte es ein Plus von revidiert 0,1 Prozent gegeben. Zunächst war eine Stagnation gemeldet worden. Der Ausstoß der Industrie stieg im September um 0,3 Prozent. Experten hatten mit diesem Zuwachs gerechnet, nach einem Rückgang um revidiert 0,2 Prozent im August. Auf den Industriesektor entfallen in den USA 9,4 Prozent der Wirtschaftsleistung. Im jüngst veröffentlichten Konjunkturbericht "Beige Book" der Federal Reserve heißt es, die Unternehmen behielten für die kommenden Monate weiter einen positiven Wirtschaftsausblick bei. Die Erwartungen deuteten jedoch eher auf ein leichtes Wachstum hin, das durch anhaltende Unsicherheiten belastet werde.

item.title: Martinez available for Leeds trip after Man United criticism, Carrick says
item.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez will be available for Sunday's Premier League game at Leeds United after the club accepted his apology for criticising its transfer policy, manager Michael Carrick said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez will be available for Sunday's Premier League game at Leeds United after the club accepted his apology for criticising its transfer policy, manager Michael Carrick said. Martinez [USN:L8N4612C3 TEXT:"met Carrick and senior club officials"] on Thursday, two days after suggesting United needed greater investment to compete at the highest level following their 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid. The centre back later apologised for his remarks and Carrick sought to downplay the episode when he spoke to reporters on Friday. "We've moved on from that. It was one of those things. It's really not a drama for the group," Carrick said. "The squad have trained really well and they are in good spirits. There is a freshness about the group... "He's part of the squad (for Sunday)." The Argentina international had singled out director of football Jason Wilcox [USN:L1N46016X TEXT:"in the post-game interview"], saying United needed more signings to compete with their rivals and build a squad capable of challenging in Europe. Martinez made the comments at a difficult time for United, who sit 13th in the Premier League table after winning only one of their opening six matches in their worst start in 40 years. The manager said the club had accepted Martinez's apology. "He's released his statement and realised he made a mistake. That's enough for us to move on with," Carrick said. "I understand the emotion. We ask for passion. There's a way of doing that and that's been acknowledged. But we need to carry that passion in the right way." Carrick, appointed permanently in May after overseeing the club's revival last season, has come under pressure following a poor start to the campaign, but said belief within the dressing room remained intact. "I don't need results. We all need results. It's bigger than me... it's not about any individual player. It's about a football club," Carrick said. "There's a lot of people saying a lot of things. That doesn't mean you know what's going on here. "That doesn't distract us from what we are creating here as a group." United travel to seventh-placed Leeds seeking their first victory in more than a month.

item.title: Technische Panne legt Flugverkehr in Italien teilweise lahm
item.description: Eine technische Störung bei der italienischen Flugsicherung hat am Freitag zu erheblichen Verspätungen und Ausfällen im ganzen Land geführt. Die Flugsicherheitsbehörde ENAV teilte mit, dass es in der Nacht zu Unregelmäßigkeiten im Datenübertragungsnetz gekommen sei. Ein Fremdverschulden schlossen die Behörden aus. ENAV habe daraufhin vorübergehende Beschränkungen für die Kapazität des Flugverkehrs eingeführt.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eine technische Störung bei der italienischen Flugsicherung hat am Freitag zu erheblichen Verspätungen und Ausfällen im ganzen Land geführt. Die Flugsicherheitsbehörde ENAV teilte mit, dass es in der Nacht zu Unregelmäßigkeiten im Datenübertragungsnetz gekommen sei. Ein Fremdverschulden schlossen die Behörden aus. ENAV habe daraufhin vorübergehende Beschränkungen für die Kapazität des Flugverkehrs eingeführt. Nach Angaben des Luftfahrtanalyse-Unternehmens Cirium wurden bis zum Vormittag 192 Flüge gestrichen. Zudem seien nur rund 31 Prozent der Flüge von italienischen Flughäfen pünktlich gestartet. An den wichtigen Drehkreuzen Mailand-Malpensa und Rom-Fiumicino seien es mit 25 und 28 Prozent sogar noch weniger gewesen. Die Betreiber der Flughäfen in Rom und Mailand warnten die Passagiere vor möglichen Verspätungen und Ausfällen und rieten ihnen, sich mit ihrer Fluggesellschaft in Verbindung zu setzen. Die Behörde ENAV (ENAV.MI) teilte weiter mit, es sei gelungen, 75 Prozent der operativen Kapazität der Flughäfen über ein sekundäres Satellitennetz wiederherzustellen. Man arbeite weiter mit den Zulieferern zusammen, um die volle Funktionsfähigkeit des primären Datennetzes wiederherzustellen. Der Flughafenbetreiber in Mailand wies zudem darauf hin, dass ein 24-stündiger Streik des Kabinenpersonals der Billigfluglinie EasyJet (EZJ.L) zu weiteren Beeinträchtigungen im Reiseverkehr führen könnte.

item.title: 米輸入物価、9月は＋1.1％で予想上回る 中東情勢でインフレ圧力拡大
item.description: [ワシントン １６日 ロイター] - 米労働省労働統計局が１６日に発表した９月の輸入物価指数は前月比１．１％上昇した...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米輸入物価、9月は＋1.1％で予想上回る　中東情勢でインフレ圧力拡大 22:39 配信

米カリフォルニア州ロングビーチ港で７月撮影。REUTERS/Mario Anzuoni

[ワシントン １６日 ロイター] - 米労働省労働統計局が１６日に発表した９月の輸入物価指数は前月比１．１％上昇した。エネルギー製品や幅広い品目のコスト上昇を背景に、市場予想（０．８％上昇）を上回る伸びとなった。中東紛争の長期化を受けて、インフレ圧力が高まっていることを改めて示唆した。

８月分は当初発表の０．７％上昇から０．５％上昇に下方改定された。

９月は前年比では８．１％上昇と、２０２２年７月以来の大幅な伸びとなった。

今週発表された消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）と卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ）はいずれも大幅な伸びを示しており、エコノミストの間ではインフレがエネルギー部門を超えて波及しているとの見方が強まっている。米国・イラン戦争が長期化する中、サプライチェーン（供給網）は混乱し、原油価格は高止まりしている。

item.title: ONU diz que avanços contra desnutrição em Gaza ficam comprometidos com interrupção de suprimentos comerciais
item.description: Os avanços no combate à desnutrição em Gaza continuam frágeis e podem ser prejudicados por interrupções no abastecimento ao enclave palestino, afirmou na sexta-feira o Unicef, agência da ONU para a infância, pedindo para que todos os pontos de passagem permaneçam abertos.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Os avanços no combate à desnutrição em Gaza continuam frágeis e podem ser prejudicados por interrupções no abastecimento ao enclave palestino, afirmou na sexta-feira o Unicef, agência da ONU para a infância, pedindo para que todos os pontos de passagem permaneçam abertos. Israel informou na quarta-feira que mercadorias comerciais não estavam mais entrando em Gaza devido ao que descreveu como uma disputa sobre impostos entre comerciantes locais e o grupo militante Hamas. Isso cortou uma fonte vital de alimentos e outros bens em um território onde a maioria depende de assistência humanitária após três anos de guerra, deslocamentos repetidos e restrições rigorosas impostas por Israel às entregas de ajuda. Embora o cessar-fogo tenha melhorado o acesso à ajuda e reduzido os combates em grande escala, as agências humanitárias afirmam que os ataques contínuos, os deslocamentos contínuos e a destruição generalizada deixaram os civis altamente vulneráveis. Em declarações à imprensa em Genebra, o porta-voz do Unicef Ricardo Pires disse que o fluxo de suprimentos comerciais e humanitários precisa permanecer previsível e contínuo. “O impacto sobre as crianças, obviamente, será sentido se essa situação não for resolvida”, declarou ele. “Não podemos voltar a uma situação em que crianças e famílias não estejam recebendo todos os suprimentos, bens e serviços de que necessitam.” O Unicef também pediu melhorias nas condições de vida no enclave amplamente devastado, onde cerca de 800 mil crianças ainda estão deslocadas e a maioria vive em barracas ou prédios inseguros com a aproximação do inverno, afirmando que melhores abrigos e serviços básicos são essenciais para apoiar uma recuperação duradoura.

item.title: Energy prices loom over EU summit
item.description: The European Union’s busy summit takes the focus in today’s newsletter as the bloc tackles how to tame soaring energy prices, imports of electric vehicles from China and emissions rules.
item.dc:creator: Sharon Kimathi
item.content:encoded: The European Union’s busy summit takes the focus in today’s newsletter as the bloc tackles how to tame soaring energy prices, imports of electric vehicles from China and emissions rules. Before we get into all the EU summit discussions, I’d like to thank readers for your positive feedback about the series on data centres. The Reuters team also sends its best wishes to one of our leading climate correspondents, Kate Abnett , whose reporting has been a cornerstone of this newsletter, as she embarks on a new chapter in her career. Now, back to the EU summit in Brussels where members of the bloc put [USN:L6N46017V TEXT:"high energy prices"] on the agenda. The summit takes place at a time of heightened economic anxiety, with fuel price spikes since the Iran and Russia-Ukraine wars put cash-strapped governments on the back foot. Meanwhile, [USN:L8N4620HY TEXT:"Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery"] after President Volodymyr Zelenskiy declared that Kyiv was abandoning a ceasefire covering energy sites announced by US President Donald Trump. [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"Click here"] to revisit the Russia energy deal. The leaders from the EU's 27 members also discussed their recent [USN:P8N43T0CW TEXT:"agreement with Beijing"] to limit imports of hybrid cars from China, a first step towards cutting a goods trade deficit that hit €360 billion ($400 billion) in 2025. They discussed the [USN:B5N443015 TEXT:"Franco-German proposals"], a joint package targeting EU automotive emissions, industrial policy, and the UK's participation in European manufacturing rules, which they released last week. The proposals mark a sharp turn for Germany, which only two years ago was the most vocal critic of EU anti-subsidy tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles. Under the [USN:L6N46119A TEXT:"plan"], which still needs to be confirmed, the automotive sector’s "Made in Europe" label would cover the EU's 27 countries and other European partners that were part of the EU internal market on January 1, 2020. That would include Britain, which left the EU single market at the end of 2020. It also waters down the CO2 emissions target for cars which would see it drop by 90% from 2021 levels in 2035. The softened target is broadly in line with the wishes of German automakers. The EU’s two largest economies, France and Germany, also said there was an urgent need for measures to deal with imports of chemicals and PET — the plastic widely used in packaging — and called for measures to retaliate quickly against countries that harm the bloc. CLIMATE BUZZ AMOC: Atlantic Ocean currents can recover from severe climate weakening The [USN:L6N45Y0O8 TEXT:"Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation"] (AMOC) system, weakened by global warming, could recover over time if the climate cools, according to a study by the Danish Meteorological Institute. The study found no sign there was an irreversible tipping point for the AMOC, as suggested by some previous studies. It also showed that the Greenland ice sheet, which contributes to weakening the AMOC as it pours cold freshwater into the ocean, could not be restored once it had melted, even if the warming trend was reversed. Turtles offer early warning from a warming Mediterranean ahead of COP31 The loggerhead turtle, which nests on shores across the Mediterranean, is the mascot of COP31, the annual UN climate summit that Turkey hosts next month. Marine conservation will be a key focus of the gathering along the coast in Antalya. Researchers say the turtle illustrates how climate change is altering ecosystems in the Mediterranean, which has experienced a long-term warming trend since the early 1980s. [USN:L6N45X02J TEXT:"Click here"] for the full in-depth report. Fires surge in Brazil's Amazon, fuelled by El Niño and climate change There were [USN:L6N45Z13X TEXT:"1,679 fires in Brazil's Amazonas"] state in the first two weeks of October, a 253% surge compared with the same period last year, according to data from the country's Amazon surveillance system. August and September are usually the height of the dry season in the Amazon, before the rainy season's onset usually brings relief in October. But rains have been slow to bring relief this year. Scientists and officials point to the El Niño phenomenon, which is predicted to be the strongest on record, and climate change as drivers of the surge in fires. Rotting meat smell sparks protest at Mexico's screwworm sterile-fly plant A rotten smell, described by residents as “[USN:L6N4611EC TEXT:"pungent in your nose and mouth"]” and causing nausea, has been hanging over a town in Mexico's southern Chiapas state this week. The odour drove residents into the streets to demand the removal of a sterile-fly plant at the centre of the US-Mexico fight against the flesh-eating New World screwworm parasite. Mexico has recorded nearly 48,000 cases of screwworm in the current outbreak and the United States 53. The Metapa plant is expected eventually to produce 100 million sterile flies a week. A spokesperson for Mexico's Agriculture Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Shippers' demand for lower-carbon marine fuels cools as IMO rules hang in balance [USN:L4N45V0CW TEXT:"International Maritime Organization"] (IMO) member nations are set to meet by early November on the formal adoption of a net-zero framework to guide the industry towards zero carbon emissions by 2050, after last year's vote to delay the move. Demand for marine biofuel, a more readily available alternative fuel, has softened this year at the world's largest bunker hub of Singapore. WHAT TO WATCH Click here for a wider image report on how the Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI) rehabilitation centre in the jungles of Indonesian Borneo is taking in more orangutans as the country’s worst wildfires in a decade sweep through the forest home of the critically endangered animals. From January to July this year, fires burned around 202,000 hectares (500,000 acres) in Indonesia. CLIMATE COMMENTARY Global ocean protection stands at roughly 10%, falling well short of the 30% international goal. Click here to find out whether nations around the world can still meet their 2030 nature protection targets in a piece by Ethical Corp Magazine contributor Mark Hillsdon . The global shift to electric vehicles might appear unstoppable, but the path there is far from straightforward, according to Reuters global energy transition columnist Gavin Maguire . [USN:L1N45Y0RF TEXT:"Click here"] to read more about what it means for the future of oil demand for road transport. Climate Lens Indonesia haze: [USN:L6N4610CY TEXT:"Emissions from the wildfires"] have been the highest in the world for a month, making up almost half the global total over the last seven days, according to data from Fire Emissions Watch, a portal developed by the European Union's Copernicus climate monitoring service. The fires have been raging for months and hundreds of thousands of people have contracted respiratory illnesses in the worst-hit provinces, [USN:L6N4560JQ TEXT:"health ministry data shows"], while the transboundary haze has also hampered air quality in neighbouring countries, forcing school closures in Malaysia and East Timor. NUMBER OF THE WEEK $2 billion That’s the top of the range of estimated [USN:L4N45Z1OP TEXT:"insured losses to onshore property"] from Hurricane Isaias, according to data analytics firm Verisk.

item.title: Italian banks should be predators not prey in M&A wave, economy minister says
item.description: Italian banks should be predators rather than prey, Economy Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti said on Friday, commenting on the M&A wave reshaping the banking sectors in Italy and Germany.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italian banks should be predators rather than prey, Economy Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti said on Friday, commenting on the M&A wave reshaping the banking sectors in Italy and Germany. Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the G7 and G20 meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, Giorgetti welcomed [USN:L6N4620CO TEXT:"ECB approval"] for UniCredit's (CRDI.MI) acquisition of Germany's Commerzbank (CBKG.DE) "Now there will be a lot of work to do to complete the transaction," Italian news agencies quoted him as saying UniCredit secured ECB approval to take delivery of the Commerzbank shares tendered into its €45 billion ($51 billion) offer, advancing plans for what would be Europe's biggest cross-border banking deal since the global financial crisis Officials have previously told Reuters that Italy's government would support UniCredit's efforts to build a large European banking group, provided the Milan-based bank keeps its [USN:L8N4151CN TEXT:"headquarters in Italy"] Asked whether Rome would also accept a cross-border deal in which a major Italian bank was the takeover target, Giorgetti said: "I would prefer an Italian bank" to be the buyer France's Credit Agricole (CAGR.PA) said [USN:L8N45U0BR TEXT:"this month"] it would not tender its 29.3% stake in Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) into Monte dei Paschi di Siena's (BMPS.MI) takeover offer The French bank has also expressed interest in a merger between its Italian unit and Banco BPM, of which it is the largest shareholder Italy has "golden powers" that allow the government to set conditions on deals involving strategic sectors such as banking, although Rome has said it will remain neutral on the current wave of M&A Separately, Giorgetti said banks, insurers and other financial institutions would be asked to help fund [USN:L8N46108R TEXT:"next year's budget"], without giving further details. ($1 = 0.8894 euros)

item.title: Central bankers eye higher rates as AI boom fuels scramble for cash
item.description: The artificial intelligence boom is setting off a global race for money, forcing central bankers to contemplate a future in which interest rates stay higher and governments need to tighten their belts after an era of largesse.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Canepa, Leika Kihara, Rae Wee
item.content:encoded: The artificial intelligence [USN:L1N45C04W TEXT:"boom"] is setting off a global race for money, forcing central bankers to contemplate a future in which interest rates stay higher and governments need to tighten their belts after an era of largesse. From silicon chips and data centres to power grids and telecoms networks, governments and companies are pouring money into projects tied directly or indirectly to AI, adding fuel to the global economy and [USN:L1N45V0NY TEXT:"pushing up borrowing costs"]. Central bankers from the world's largest economies gathering in Bangkok said the boom was also creating fresh inflation pressures and financial risks, because the investment is arriving long before the productivity gains AI promises. "If you're a central banker...you've got to recognise this as a shock," Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said at the [USN:L1N4620A6 TEXT:"annual meetings"] of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok. "It's obviously hitting the demand side of the economy before it's going to hit the supply side." Warsh, who said the US was benefiting from a broadening "surge of investment", warned the transition could be "very bumpy" as investors, companies and policymakers grappled with a technology whose ultimate winners remain unclear. Several of his colleagues from the G20 group of large economies also in the Thai capital said it would only take a slight reassessment of the rosy earnings prospects underpinning AI investments to cause profound market ructions, as a [USN:L1N461090 TEXT:"selloff in Asian tech stocks"] showed this week. STARS BEHIND THE CLOUDS The debate marks a striking shift from the years following the 2008 financial crisis, when policymakers worried about excess global savings and inflation that was persistently too low. Now central bankers increasingly see the opposite problem: too much demand for capital. "There is a global fight for money," ECB policymaker Martins Kazaks told Reuters. "Investment in AI is one of the key factors driving up the cost of money." That pressure is being amplified by governments from the United States to Japan and Germany borrowing heavily for defence, industrial policy and energy projects. For central bankers, the implication is that the level of interest rates needed to keep economies on an even keel, known as R-star, may be rising. "The problem at the moment in calculating the R-star is that the stars are covered by the clouds, and the clouds are so thick," South African Reserve Bank Governor Lesetja Kganyago said. "We know that R-star is higher, but we do not know how high." A higher neutral rate means the same level of interest rate is less restrictive than previously thought. "Maybe rates, on average, will be that little bit higher," said Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill. The Bank of Japan has already cited AI-related demand as a factor behind its recent rate increases, arguing that investment-driven price pressures have become broader and more persistent. Economists expect the Bank of England to raise rates at its next meeting on November 5. The ECB and Fed raised rates in September, and markets have priced in another move by them both in December. NO MORE CHEAP MONEY The prospect of structurally higher borrowing costs poses a challenge for governments that built up large debts during years when interest rates hovered near zero. Sovereign bond yields have [USN:L8N45N0KW TEXT:"risen across the world"], and in recent weeks some have reached levels not seen since before the global financial crisis. The euro zone, and notably [USN:L1N45N0CH TEXT:"debt-laden France"], was seen as particularly exposed. Much of the AI-driven investment surge is taking place in the United States and, to a lesser extent, Japan and other parts of Asia, with [USN:L6N4610HN TEXT:"ASML"] and Siemens among the few clear European winners. Meanwhile, the bloc faces higher energy costs from wars in Iran and Ukraine , compounding inflation pressures and squeezing public finances. "There are particular circumstances that lead to some countries being more affected, France being a case in point," ECB President Christine Lagarde said at a CNN event in Bangkok. "And for that one, the primary and first solution lies at home in France. And it has to do with fiscal policies."

item.title: Miles de personas marchan en la capital albanesa mientras se extienden protestas contra el Gobierno
item.description: Miles de jóvenes albaneses se manifestaron el viernes por Tirana, rompiendo algunas ventanas y semáforos en el cuarto día de una campaña liderada por estudiantes, cada vez más violenta, para obligar al primer ministro Edi Rama a dimitir.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Miles de jóvenes albaneses se manifestaron el viernes por Tirana, rompiendo algunas ventanas y semáforos en el cuarto día de una campaña liderada por estudiantes, cada vez más violenta, para obligar al primer ministro Edi Rama a dimitir. Las manifestaciones, que se están extendiendo por todo el país, se convirtieron el jueves en disturbios en la capital, donde los manifestantes rompieron escaparates, asaltaron un banco y se enfrentaron a la policía. Estas protestas llegan tras meses de manifestaciones en su mayoría pacíficas que, según los estudiantes, el Gobierno ignoró. "Nos están llevando al límite", dijo Enea, un manifestante de 19 años que se negó a dar su apellido por miedo a ser detenido. Dijo que su mensaje para Rama era: "Que renuncie lo antes posible antes de que todo se vaya al traste". Los estudiantes acusan a los funcionarios de corrupción y de descuidar la educación, y dicen estar indignados por la venta de tramos vírgenes de la costa albanesa a un complejo turístico de lujo respaldado por Jared Kushner, yerno del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump. Los disturbios suponen un reto para Rama, que el año pasado ganó su cuarto mandato con la promesa de llevar a Albania a la Unión Europea y que aspira a que el país se incorpore a la UE ya en 2028. "No cederemos ante la violencia", dijo en Facebook. LAS EMPRESAS PIDEN A LOS MANIFESTANTES QUE LAS DEJEN EN PAZ Los estudiantes, muchos de ellos con máscaras, se enfrentaron a las filas de la policía antidisturbios frente al edificio del Ministerio de Educación. Algunas pequeñas empresas tenían las persianas bajadas y notas en sus fachadas que decían: "Estamos con ustedes. No dañén nuestros negocios por toda la ciudad". En la localidad costera de Lezha, la policía se enfrentó a manifestantes que lanzaban piedras. Las protestas también se han extendido a Elbasan, Skhodra y Korca, donde los manifestantes rompieron ventanas e incendiaron contenedores de basura, informaron los medios locales. "Llevamos 140 días protestando pacíficamente y nadie nos ha escuchado. Así que esta es nuestra única oportunidad de hacernos oír y conseguir los derechos que nos merecemos", dijo una manifestante de 19 años que solo se identificó como Klea. Las manifestaciones se desencadenaron por los planes de construir el complejo turístico, que se ha enfrentado a impugnaciones legales. Los vecinos del pueblo declararon a Reuters en julio que sus terrenos se habían vendido indebidamente para su urbanización. Posteriormente, Reuters informó que el hombre que vendió los terrenos era buscado por la fiscalía por tráfico de drogas, acusaciones que su abogado negó. Reuters no encontró pruebas de irregularidades por parte de Kushner, quien no está directamente implicado en el conflicto de los vecinos. El analista político Afrim Krasniqi dijo que las generaciones más jóvenes no ven futuro en Albania. "Ven que todos los recursos del país —políticos, económicos, todo— están en manos de los oligarcas", dijo a Reuters. Los escándalos de corrupción han empañado la imagen de Albania a lo largo de los años y los analistas dicen que el país es un centro neurálgico para las bandas que buscan blanquear dinero procedente del tráfico de drogas y armas, lo que complica sus esfuerzos por incorporarse a la UE. Junto con Montenegro, Albania lidera el proceso de adhesión entre los países balcánicos. Los disturbios forman parte de una ola de activismo estudiantil en Europa. En Francia, los estudiantes de secundaria llevan semanas organizando protestas y bloqueos en los centros educativos para exigir más profesores y mejores instalaciones, argumentando que el deterioro de los edificios escolares y el hacinamiento en las aulas están socavando la educación.

item.title: Microdramas are set to upstage Hollywood's A-list
item.description: ReelShort and other apps offering two-minute video serials rival Netflix and Disney for views. Low costs and smartphone users explain the success of series like "Rejecting My Five Female Mates". After taking China by storm, the format spells more gloom for Tinseltown incumbents.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Saba
item.content:encoded: Netflix founder Reed Hastings once ruminated that the streaming service’s true competitor was sleep. The latest cultural craze that has emerged from China poses a different challenge. Microdramas are gaining ground and rivaling Hollywood incumbents for time and attention. The short episodic vertical videos, each lasting around two minutes, are sweeping the United States. The format is a distant cousin of the soap opera — popular themes include love, money and jealousy — tailor-made for easily distracted smartphone addicts. The series show up on social media networks like TikTok and Instagram and are also available on dedicated apps like ReelShort and DramaBox. Viewers are gripped. The series “Found a Homeless Billionaire Husband for Christmas,” racked up more than 400 million views, per research firm Omdia, rivaling the record-breaking 500 million views achieved by Netflix’s “KPop Demon Hunters” in the first six months after its release. YouTube said microdramas surpassed 6.5 billion views on the video platform in the first half of 2026 alone, while time spent watching the shows jumped 50% year-over-year. They are oddly compelling. Dedicated apps hook viewers with a few free episodes and then present a menu of paid options to watch the rest, ranging from pay-per-view coins to yearly subscriptions. ReelShort's “ The Counterattack of the Fat Wife Queen ," is schlocky and borderline absurd. Yet after watching the first 10 short episodes, this columnist almost broke out the corporate credit card to access the final 47. Low expenses add to the appeal for producers. A microdrama series costs somewhere in [USN:L6N44B0T8 TEXT:"the ballpark"] of $300,000, a fraction of the outlay for a regular soap opera or half-hour sitcom. Artificial intelligence further reduces overheads. In the People’s Republic, where short dramas known as duanju took off around 2020, 95% of those released in the first quarter of this year were AI generated, according to analysts at MoffettNathanson. The format has reached such prominence in Tinseltown that the main union representing actors felt compelled to roll out rules and guidelines to protect members working on set. Previous attempts to develop vertical video struggled. The most high-profile flop was Jeffrey Katzenberg and Meg Whitman’s Quibi, which launched in 2020 but failed after burning through almost $2 billion. Yet this time users, conditioned to consume short-form videos by TikTok, may be more willing. Projections for microdrama revenue are still relatively micro: the format is set to bring in $1.5 billion this year, per Omdia. In China, however, it has hit $9 billion in revenue, surpassing the $7 billion spent on cinema tickets. If the same trend holds stateside, microdramas could eventually overtake the almost $9 billion collected by US and Canadian box offices last year. Such rapid growth would eat into entertainment budgets, squeezing Netflix (NFLX.O) and other streamers such as Walt Disney (DIS.N) , which already face a slowdown. Another incumbent, movie studio Skydance (SKYD.N) , is busy with the challenge of absorbing Warner Bros. Small but mighty microdramas are ready to elbow aside Hollywood's A-list. Follow Jennifer Saba on Bluesky and LinkedIn . CONTEXT NEWS YouTube said on September 23 that so-called microdramas surpassed 6.5 billion views in the first half of 2026 and that vertical shorts on TV increased by over 90% year-over-year for the same period. Netflix co-Chief Executive Ted Sarandos said at an industry conference on September 30 that the streaming service was not growing as fast as he would like.

item.title: Trump dice que EEUU podría verse obligado a atacar la montaña Pickaxe, en Irán
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo que su país podría verse obligado a atacar la montaña Pickaxe, una instalación vinculada al programa nuclear de Irán, en su intento por garantizar que Teherán no consiga un arma nuclear.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo que su país podría verse obligado a atacar la montaña Pickaxe, una instalación vinculada al programa nuclear de Irán, en su intento por garantizar que Teherán no consiga un arma nuclear. En una entrevista concedida a Newsmax en la noche del jueves, Trump también afirmó que no utilizaría un arma nuclear en la guerra contra Irán, que comenzó en febrero con los ataques conjuntos de Estados Unidos e Israel. Trump afirmó que Estados Unidos quería asegurarse de que Irán nunca disponga de un arma nuclear "porque, si la tuvieran, la utilizarían". "Su instalación nuclear está enterrada bajo millones de toneladas de montaña. Ahora estamos fijándonos en la montaña Pickaxe. Puede que tengamos que ir allí. Lo intentaremos. La destruiremos con rapidez", declaró Trump a Newsmax. La montaña Pickaxe es una instalación fortificada situada a gran profundidad bajo tierra, cerca de una de las principales instalaciones nucleares de Teherán. Trump afirmó que no hay necesidad de utilizar una bomba nuclear en Irán. "No utilizaría armas nucleares. No tenemos por qué hacerlo", señaló. Asimismo, reiteró que no está barajando el despliegue de tropas terrestres estadounidenses en Irán. Trump no precisó si había autorizado el uso de la bomba GBU-43/B, también conocida como la "madre de todas las bombas", contra las infraestructuras energéticas y las instalaciones nucleares iraníes. Sí afirmó que no es una bomba nuclear.

item.title: Medvedev sees off Paul to set up Shanghai semi with comeback king Jodar
item.description: Former world number one Daniil Medvedev downed Tommy Paul 6-3 1-6 6-3 in the Shanghai Masters quarter-finals on Friday, while Spaniard Rafael Jodar toppled Casper Ruud 4-6 6-4 6-3 to become the youngest semi-finalist in the tournament's history.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former world number one Daniil Medvedev downed Tommy Paul 6-3 1-6 6-3 in the Shanghai Masters quarter-finals on Friday, while Spaniard Rafael Jodar toppled Casper Ruud 4-6 6-4 6-3 to become the youngest semi-finalist in the tournament's history. Russian fifth seed Medvedev fired 16 aces and 31 winners in a two-hour and eight-minute contest against the 15th-seeded American to reach the 70th tour-level semi of his career and strengthen his bid for a place at the ATP Finals in Turin. The 30-year-old regrouped after dropping the second set and took control in the decider, capitalising on a dip in Paul's level to improve to 5-1 in their career meetings. Medvedev next faces Jodar for the first time, while twice Grand Slam champion and top seed Alexander Zverev meets Spaniard Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the other semi-final. "He has a great game," Medvedev said of Jodar. "He hits very strong, so it is going to be fun to see it in real life, to get the feel. "If I am playing well, I am tough to beat and that is what I am going to try to do." Medvedev won his third title of the season in Hangzhou last month and is the only former Shanghai champion remaining in the draw, having lifted the trophy in 2019. JODAR'S RISE CONTINUES Jodar, 20, secured his fourth consecutive comeback victory from a set down at the ATP Masters 1000 event, extending a dream run on his Shanghai debut. The 12th seed broke 20th-seeded Norwegian Ruud five times across the final two sets to wrest control of a tight encounter. After seizing the crucial break for 5-4 in the second set and serving it out to love, Jodar elevated his game in the decider, breaking the former world number two Ruud three more times to seal victory in two hours and 20 minutes. The latest milestone in Jodar's breakthrough season also strengthened his chances of qualifying for the ATP Finals in his first full year on the ATP Tour. Ranked 903 in the world little more than a year ago, Jodar surged into the top 50 in April after capturing his [USN:L4N40P05R TEXT:"maiden ATP title in Morocco"] and reaching the [USN:L6N411045 TEXT:"semi-finals in Barcelona"]. The energetic and aggressive right-hander built on that momentum with quarter-final appearances in Madrid and Rome before making the last eight at the French Open, where eventual champion Zverev ended his run. Shanghai marks Jodar's fifth tour-level semi-final of the season and his second at Masters 1000 level after Montreal. "I'm super happy how the season is going," Jodar said. "Very high level, but still a lot of things to improve, which is very good because that means I can become a better player in the future. I just want more things. "It's the first year on Tour and there are still a few tournaments, so I will try to give my best in the matches I have left this season."

item.title: Estrela verde recém-identificada deixa astrônomos maravilhados
item.description: Pela primeira vez, astrônomos identificaram uma estrela verde, registrando um denso remanescente estelar chamado anã branca que adquiriu um tom fantasmagórico de verde-amarelado após absorver detritos rochosos de planetas que outrora haviam orbitado em torno dela.
item.dc:creator: Will Dunham
item.content:encoded: Pela primeira vez, astrônomos identificaram uma estrela verde, registrando um denso remanescente estelar chamado anã branca que adquiriu um tom fantasmagórico de verde-amarelado após absorver detritos rochosos de planetas que outrora haviam orbitado em torno dela. A cor de uma estrela é normalmente determinada por sua temperatura: as estrelas mais frias apresentam uma cor alaranjada, o Sol e estrelas semelhantes a ele aparecem brancas, e as mais quentes apresentam um tom azul claro. Mas a regra é diferente para uma anã branca, que é o núcleo remanescente de uma estrela de massa baixa a média que esgotou seu combustível nuclear e expeliu suas camadas externas. A maioria das anãs brancas tem cores semelhantes às de outras estrelas, e sua cor média é o branco. Mas mudanças em sua composição química ao longo do tempo podem transformar algumas delas em cores mais raras. A anã branca verde recém-identificada, chamada WD J1330+6435, é uma anã branca na Via Láctea localizada a cerca de 280 anos-luz da Terra, na constelação de Draco. Um ano-luz é a distância que a luz percorre em um ano, ou seja, 9,5 trilhões de km. “Começamos a nos interessar por essa anã branca porque fragmentos de material planetário caíram em sua superfície, enriquecendo suas camadas externas com elementos como cálcio, lítio e, em particular, sódio”, disse o astrofísico Mark Hollands, da Universidade de Warwick, na Inglaterra, principal autor do estudo publicado na revista RAS Techniques and Instruments. Em estrelas normais, o sódio absorve um comprimento de onda muito específico de cor laranja — o mesmo tom de laranja que dá às lâmpadas de sódio de rua sua cor característica. “Nessa anã branca em particular, no entanto, a densidade é tão alta que os átomos de sódio são constantemente bombardeados por átomos de hélio ao redor, o que altera os níveis de energia atômica do sódio”, disse Hollands. “O resultado final é que os átomos de sódio não absorvem mais um comprimento de onda muito estreito de laranja — eles absorvem os comprimentos de onda amarelos, laranjas e alguns dos vermelhos. E o que resta é uma estrela que possui um belo brilho verde-amarelado, algo que não seria possível para estrelas semelhantes ao Sol”, disse Hollands. A descoberta fez parte de um projeto que avaliava a cor das anãs brancas tal como os olhos humanos as veriam. Uma anã branca normalmente tem metade da massa do Sol compactada no tamanho da Terra. “Como as anãs brancas são estrelas superdensas — têm aproximadamente o tamanho da Terra, mas contêm cerca de 165 mil vezes a sua massa —, mesmo uma pequena quantidade de sódio bloqueia grande parte da luz laranja que emana da estrela”, disse Boris Gänsicke, astrofísico da Universidade de Warwick e coautor do estudo. “No fim das contas, tudo isso é muito semelhante à mistura de cores na paleta de um pintor. Eles começam com algumas cores básicas e, em seguida, as misturam para formar qualquer cor necessária para sua pintura. Retire parte da cor que entra na mistura e o resultado final mudará”, disse Gänsicke. (Reportagem de Will Dunham)

item.title: FMI-L'Europe doit stimuler la croissance ou emprunter moins pour garantir la viabilité de sa dette
item.description: L'Europe doit croître plus rapidement ou emprunter moins pour maintenir sa dette sur une trajectoire viable, a déclaré vendredi le Fonds monétaire international (FMI), soulignant que les plans de redressement prévus pourraient ne pas être suffisants.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski
item.content:encoded: L'Europe doit croître plus rapidement ou emprunter moins pour maintenir sa dette sur une trajectoire viable, a déclaré vendredi le Fonds monétaire international (FMI), soulignant que les plans de redressement prévus pourraient ne pas être suffisants. "Environ les trois quarts des pays européens auront besoin d'une combinaison de réformes structurelles, visant à stimuler la croissance et à alléger les pressions sur les dépenses, ainsi que de mesures d'assainissement budgétaire visant à réduire le déficit d'environ 3,5% du PIB en moyenne, à moyen terme, afin de maintenir la viabilité de la dette", a déclaré l'institution financière dans un rapport consacré à l'Europe. Le redressement budgétaire prévu dans le cadre des plans à moyen terme de l'UE, sur lesquels chaque pays a dû s'accorder avec la Commission européenne, s'élève en moyenne à environ 2% du PIB, ce qui est inférieur à ce qui sera nécessaire pour certains pays, a également averti le FMI. "Environ un quart des pays européens devraient procéder à un assainissement budgétaire de plus de 5% du PIB pour maintenir la viabilité de la dette publique, ce qui dépasse ce qui s'est généralement avéré faisable par le passé, ne laissant d'autre choix que de repenser la portée de l'action publique et de renforcer le rôle du secteur privé pour combler le déficit", a-t-il ajouté. Le FMI prévoit une croissance économique de 1,1% cette année dans le bloc, une estimation révisée à la hausse par rapport à celle publiée en juillet (0,9%), mais inchangée par rapport à celle d'avril dernier, grâce à une hausse des investissements dans l'intelligence artificielle (IA) et à l'augmentation des dépenses de défense. Il prévoit également que l'inflation dans les 21 pays de la zone euro s'élèvera à 3,1% cette année, à 2,8% en 2027 et à 2,2% en 2028. Les projections de la Commission européenne datant du mois de mai montrent un ratio dette/PIB de l'UE passant de 82,8% à la fin de 2025 à 84,2% en 2026, puis à 85,3% d'ici 2027. Dans la zone euro, la dette devrait passer de 88,7% du PIB en 2025 à 90,2% en 2026, puis atteindre 91,2% en 2027. "La dette publique pourrait augmenter considérablement, jusqu'à doubler son niveau actuel dans l'économie européenne moyenne si aucune mesure n'est prise", a déclaré à Reuters Mateusz Szczurek, chef du département européen du FMI. Il cite des facteurs tels que le vieillissement de la population, l'augmentation des besoins en matière de défense et la poursuite de la transition énergétique pour expliquer ces prévisions. Les inquiétudes concernant la santé des finances publiques sont particulièrement pressantes en France, deuxième économie de la zone euro, qui peine à réduire ses déficits et qui, ce même mois, a vu les rendements de sa dette souveraine atteindre [USN:L6N45N0ET TEXT:"un plus haut"] depuis 2002. Selon Mateusz Szczurek, cette hausse des coûts de financement de la France est gérable à court terme, mais si elle persiste, elle accentuera la pression sur le gouvernement pour qu'il présente un plan d'assainissement crédible à moyen terme, au-delà du budget 2027. "Le marché est liquide, la structure des échéances est assez longue, la base d'investisseurs est diversifiée et la liquidité bancaire est élevée, ce qui est également un atout. Les risques liés à la dette à court terme sont donc tout à fait gérables", a-t-il déclaré. "Mais si les taux d'intérêt devaient rester élevés plus longtemps, cela exercerait une pression accrue sur les finances publiques et la maîtrise des coûts", a-t-il ajouté. Le FMI prévoit que le PIB français ne progressera que de 0,4% cette année et de 0,7% en 2027, revoyant ainsi nettement à la baisse ses prévisions d'avril, qui tablaient sur une croissance de 0,9% pour ces deux années.

item.title: Over 1 million consumers were facing power cuts in Ukraine at some point, energy ministry says
item.description: Russia continued attacking Ukrainian energy facilities in the capital Kyiv and five other regions on Friday, causing emergency power outages, Ukraine's energy ministry said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia continued attacking Ukrainian energy facilities in the capital Kyiv and five other regions on Friday, causing emergency power outages, Ukraine's energy ministry said. The ministry noted that more than 1 million consumers were facing power cuts at some point and "repair work is continuing wherever the security situation permits".

Oct 16 : New York has barely stopped celebrating its first NBA title in 53 years, and the Knicks are already chasing a repeat in a league that is built to stop one. The NBA has crowned a record eight different champions in the last eight seasons. Rules that make it tougher to stack a roster with superstars have turned the league into a free-for-all. The Knicks, however, have a big edge: the band is back together. New York returns its five best players, Jalen Brunson, Josh Hart, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns, along with the chemistry that carried it to the title. THE LEBRON PLOT TWIST

The offseason's biggest story was where the NBA's all-time leading scorer, LeBron James, would land after splitting with the Los Angeles Lakers. The surprise winner of the sweepstakes was the Philadelphia 76ers. James admitted he would have liked to play for the Knicks, but said that door closed once they won the title. So the 41-year-old will take his talents to Philadelphia instead of the Big Apple, although he will reportedly be living part-time in New York and commuting by helicopter. There he joins Jaylen Brown, who was stunningly traded by the Celtics in the offseason, along with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe. The question is whether the pieces fit, since all five players are accustomed to having the ball in their hands. "They are like a room that has five beautiful couches in it," ESPN's Brian Windhorst told ABS-CBN News. "But you don't need five couches in a room. You need a couch and a chair, a table, a TV and a mirror, and that's going to be a challenge. Can they all fit, or do you have to put one couch up along the wall." WELCOME TO THE GARDEN James could hardly have a more dramatic debut. The four-time champion opens his Philadelphia career at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday, just after the Knicks raise their championship banner. His teams have often started slowly in his first season with them. If that happens again, Philadelphia's famously impatient fans may not wait long to let everyone know how they feel. The payoff could be historic. A title in his record-extending 24th season would make James the first player to win championships with four different teams. EVERYONE ELSE WANTS IN The rest of the league has its own plans when the 2026-27 season tips off on Tuesday: • Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs want revenge after a bitter Finals loss. • Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Oklahoma City Thunder are going for a second title in three years. • Stephen Curry leads a Golden State Warriors team trying to revive its title hopes.

item.title: ONU dice avances en lucha contra desnutrición Gaza se ven amenazados por interrupción suministros comerciales
item.description: Los avances en la lucha contra la desnutrición en Gaza siguen siendo frágiles y podrían verse comprometidos por las interrupciones en el suministro de mercancías que llegan al enclave palestino, dijo el viernes UNICEF, la agencia de la ONU para la infancia, que instó a que todos los pasos fronterizos permanezcan abiertos.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Los avances en la lucha contra la desnutrición en Gaza siguen siendo frágiles y podrían verse comprometidos por las interrupciones en el suministro de mercancías que llegan al enclave palestino, dijo el viernes UNICEF, la agencia de la ONU para la infancia, que instó a que todos los pasos fronterizos permanezcan abiertos. Israel afirmó el miércoles que ya no entraban mercancías comerciales en Gaza debido a lo que describió como una disputa sobre impuestos entre los comerciantes locales y el grupo militante Hamás. Esto ha cortado una fuente vital de alimentos y otros bienes en un territorio donde la mayoría de la población depende de la ayuda humanitaria tras tres años de guerra, desplazamientos repetidos y estrictas restricciones israelíes al envío de ayuda. Aunque el alto el fuego ha mejorado el acceso a la ayuda y ha reducido los combates a gran escala, las agencias humanitarias afirman que los ataques continuos, los desplazamientos constantes y la destrucción generalizada han dejado a la población civil en una situación de gran vulnerabilidad. En declaraciones a la prensa en Ginebra, el portavoz de UNICEF, Ricardo Pires, afirmó que el flujo de suministros, tanto comerciales como humanitarios, debe seguir siendo predecible y continuo. "Es evidente que los niños sufrirán las consecuencias si esta situación no se resuelve", afirmó. "No podemos volver a una situación en la que los niños y las familias no reciban todos los suministros, bienes y servicios que necesitan". Un nuevo informe de UNICEF publicado el viernes revela que, aunque el alto el fuego vigente desde octubre ha permitido la entrada de más ayuda humanitaria y suministros comerciales, la desnutrición aguda sigue siendo un riesgo. El informe señala que los avances en la lucha contra la amenaza de hambruna, confirmados por un reporte mundial sobre seguridad alimentaria en agosto del año pasado, se han logrado gracias a una respuesta ampliada en materia de alimentación y nutrición, a la flexibilización de las restricciones a la entrada de suministros alimentarios y nutricionales, y al alto el fuego. Sin embargo, esos avances siguen siendo frágiles, según el informe. "Las tasas de desnutrición aguda han descendido, pero solo uno de cada tres niños menores de dos años alcanza actualmente la diversidad alimentaria mínima", afirma el informe. Una encuesta realizada por UNICEF en junio también reveló una prevalencia significativa de desnutrición crónica, que afecta a uno de cada ocho niños menores de cinco años. UNICEF también pidió que se mejoraran las condiciones de vida en este enclave, en gran parte devastado, donde unos 800.000 niños siguen desplazados y la mayoría vive en tiendas de campaña o en edificios inseguros a medida que se acerca el invierno, y señaló que es esencial contar con mejores alojamientos y servicios básicos para apoyar una recuperación duradera.

item.title: Polonia insta a tecnológicas a tomar medidas contra contenidos violentos tras ataques en colegios
item.description: Polonia convocó el viernes a empresas de Internet, entre ellas Google y Meta , al ministerio de Asuntos Digitales, y les exigió que tomen más medidas para frenar la difusión de contenidos violentos tras una serie de ataques con arma blanca en centros educativos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Polonia convocó el viernes a empresas de Internet, entre ellas Google (GOOGL.O) y Meta (META.O) , al ministerio de Asuntos Digitales, y les exigió que tomen más medidas para frenar la difusión de contenidos violentos tras una serie de ataques con arma blanca en centros educativos. Esta semana se han desplegado miles de agentes de policía en los colegios para garantizar la seguridad, después de que una serie de tres ataques en cuatro días desencadenó una ola de amenazas en línea que ha hecho que alumnos y profesores teman por su seguridad. Varsovia dice que la glorificación de la violencia en determinados rincones de Internet, por ejemplo en grupos dedicados a la ideología nazi o que idolatran a asesinos en serie, está teniendo un efecto perjudicial en los niños, y ha instado a las empresas de redes sociales a que redoblen sus esfuerzos para impedir la difusión de contenidos que fomenten o amenacen con la violencia. "Todos los ciudadanos polacos esperan que nadie incite a otros a suicidarse, que no haya contenidos que respalden o fomenten amenazas delictivas, y que los usuarios no se vean expuestos a situaciones como actos de asesinato, daños físicos o mutilaciones", dijo el ministro de Asuntos Digitales, Krzysztof Gawkowski, en una rueda de prensa. Gawkowski señaló que, entre el 7 y el 12 de octubre, Polonia denunció a las empresas de Internet 89 casos de contenido ilegal relacionado con los atentados y que, en dos tercios de los casos, estas no tomaron ninguna medida. A la reunión asistieron representantes de Google, Meta, TikTok, Discord y Telegram. Se invitó a X, de Elon Musk, pero no acudió, según indicó Gawkowski. Las empresas no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. El Gobierno está acelerando la tramitación de una ley para que resulte más fácil y rápido eliminar los contenidos perjudiciales. El último apuñalamiento tuvo lugar el sábado, cuando tres personas resultaron heridas en un centro de formación profesional de Varsovia. El suceso ocurrió tras un ataque el 8 de octubre en Leszczydol-Nowiny, al noreste de la capital, donde un antiguo alumno de 15 años que llevaba una cámara montada en el casco mató a un conserje del centro e hirió a dos profesores. Un día antes, un joven de 19 años hirió a diez personas, incluido él mismo, en un colegio de Ostroleka.

item.title: Rejuvenated London Metal Exchange looks to new horizons
item.description: It's that time of year when the global metals industry gathers in London for the annual blitz of trading and partying that is known as London Metal Exchange (LME) Week.
item.dc:creator: Andy Home
item.content:encoded: It's that time of year when the global metals industry gathers in London for the annual blitz of trading and partying that is known as London Metal Exchange (LME) Week. This year, visitors will find the exchange in remarkably good health. The 2022 [USN:L4N3Q30NK TEXT:"nickel crisis"] is now receding in the rear-view mirror and, as with a string of previous LME crises, the 149-year-old institution has roared back stronger than ever. The LME notched up record volumes in 2025, and this year is shaping up to be even better, with average daily turnover up 16% year-on-year from January to September. The trading boom is in part down to the exchange's market reform program , launched in response to the failings exposed by the nickel crisis. But war, tariffs and heightened investor interest in the metals sector have also played a part in the resurgence. Now fully recovered from its [USN:L8N32R32O TEXT:"near-death experience"] in 2022, the LME is setting its sights on new horizons. BRIDGING THE DIVIDE The LME will later this month [USN:S8N3LL0QW TEXT:"start trading"] a new hot-rolled-coil (HRC) Steel Shanghai contract, which will be settled against the Shanghai Futures Exchange's (ShFE) HRC contract , widely regarded as the global benchmark for the flat steel sector. It's a significant event in the world of metals trading. The cross-listing is [USN:L8N43819N TEXT:"the first time ShFE"] has made any of its metal prices available to another exchange. That it has chosen the LME attests to the thaw in relations between the two exchanges since ShFE led the fight [USN:L8N12B0UZ TEXT:"to block"] the LME's attempt to open warehouses on the Chinese mainland. The nickel crisis, however, forced the two rivals to work together with the common goal of resuming trading and restoring order to what had become a highly disorderly market. Equally symbolic of the new relationship was the opening of LME warehouses in Hong Kong last year. It's belated vindication for Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) (0388.HK) , which bought the LME in 2012 with the stated ambition of bridging the east-west divide. It's taken 14 years, but then-CEO Charles Li's vision is finally starting to take concrete form. If the new steel contract is successful, it could be a template for other products. At the very least, it may reboot the LME's ferrous portfolio. The exchange has seven steel contracts, but only three have traded this year and, bucking the broader trend, combined volumes were down 29% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026. DUBAI CONNECTOR This time last year, the LME sprang something of a surprise when it announced that HKEX would create a Dubai-based subsidiary, Commodity Pricing and Analysis Ltd (CPAL), to act as a "pricing administrator" for sustainable metal premiums. Metal premiums, sustainable or otherwise, have until now been the preserve of price reporting agencies such as Fastmarkets and S&P Global Platts, whose assessments underpin the CME's physical aluminium premium contracts. One year on, CPAL is now publishing its own price assessments for both aluminium and copper premiums in Europe under the "LME Insight" brand. The so-called "green" premium for sustainable metal brands remains elusive, but the strategy may be about to bear fruit in another part of the aluminium supply chain. Alumina, the intermediate product between bauxite and aluminium, was, until 15 or so years ago, priced as a percentage of the metal price. US producer Alcoa (AA.N) led the charge to break the linkage in favour of prices determined by spot sales. The hope was that these would become indices underpinning futures contracts. That never happened. The LME's alumina contract doesn't trade and the CME contract has seen only sporadic activity. India's Hindalco (HALC.NS) is now leading a new alumina [USN:L8N45N16J TEXT:"pricing revolution"] with a commitment to channel its spot sales through Metalshub, a digital platform for trading and pricing raw materials. Metalshub has been working with the LME on sustainable-premium price discovery and is also collaborating with CPAL. It's not difficult to join the potential dots. A new alumina price index may arrive much faster than a transaction-based "green" premium. If it does, the LME will be first in line to "futurise" it. The LME is on new ground here. No other exchange has built its own bridge between physical and futures metal pricing. But, as with the transformative tie-up with Shanghai, it's a sign that the venerable old institution has bounced back from its latest crisis with a new-found sense of purpose. (The opinions expressed here are those of Andy Home , a columnist for Reuters.) Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. item.title: Private credit roundup: CoreWeave's debt stress tests private credit's AI financing boom
item.description: Private credit's expanding role in financing AI infrastructure faced one of its clearest market tests this week as CoreWeave's bonds fell to distressed levels, raising questions about how lenders are pricing a boom built on chips, data centres and customer contracts.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Private credit's expanding role in financing AI infrastructure faced one of its clearest market tests this week as CoreWeave's bonds fell to distressed levels, raising questions about how lenders are pricing a boom built on chips, data centres and customer contracts. CoreWeave (CRWV.O) has about [USN:L4N46111C TEXT:"$50 billion of debt"], according to LSEG data, making it one of the largest borrowers linking private credit to the AI buildout. The [USN:L6N4610J0 TEXT:"cost of insuring its debt"] against default climbed to about 1,200 basis points this week, while yields on some of its bonds rose to roughly 15% to 16%, signalling sharply increased investor concern over its credit risk. James Martin, senior US credit strategist at SMBC, said investors were favoring high-yield data-centre financings for projects closer to completion and with fewer hurdles before entering service. "There is still a price. Investors are still comfortable financing it, but they're demanding more compensation for it," he said, referring to projects further from completion. Private capital has played a central role in CoreWeave's expansion. It [USN:L4N461177 TEXT:"raised"] a $2.3 billion facility in 2023 backed by graphics processing units, or GPUs, led by Magnetar Capital and Blackstone Tactical Opportunities, followed by a $7.5 billion facility in 2024 involving Blackstone, Magnetar, Carlyle, BlackRock and other investors. An $8.5 billion facility raised in March this year was anchored by Blackstone Credit & Insurance. The implications extend well beyond one borrower. Alternative asset manager Carlyle said in an October paper that private credit could be called on to finance roughly $1 trillion of the AI-compute buildout, more than half the industry's current assets under management. It warned that rapid lending into the sector could create concentration risks similar to those that emerged in software lending. "The clearest lesson is not to avoid AI compute exposure, but to set concentration limits before the buildout accelerates further, not after," Carlyle said. Some AI loans are backed not only by GPUs but also by long-term customer contracts. CoreWeave has large commitments from Microsoft (MSFT.O) , OpenAI and Meta Platforms (META.O) , while several of its financings use special-purpose vehicles tied to specific infrastructure assets and customer contracts. That can strengthen the credit by reducing lenders' reliance on the resale value of chips, but it can also create concentration risk if repayment depends heavily on a small number of large customers continuing to honour and renew those contracts. If funding costs remain elevated, lenders could demand wider spreads, lower leverage, stronger covenants and tighter limits on customer and technology concentration. Direct-lending funds [USN:L4N4610MC TEXT:"raised"] $129.15 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 35% from a year earlier and the highest nine-month total in Preqin data going back to 2016. Estimated third-quarter lending volume, however, fell 28% year on year to $49.77 billion, according to PitchBook/LCD. Competition from the syndicated loan market has also intensified. Some $16.39 billion of direct-lending loans were refinanced in the broadly syndicated market in the third quarter, compared with just $2.60 billion of syndicated loans moving into direct lending, PitchBook/LCD data showed.
