item.description: O próximo Congresso, eleito no último dia 4 de outubro, está se preparando para um embate com o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), incluindo planos para um impeachment sem precedentes de um de seus ministros, o que poderia ampliar drasticamente o alcance de uma agenda de direita, disseram à Reuters mais de uma dezena de especialistas e funcionários do Senado e do Judiciário.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: O próximo Congresso, eleito no último dia 4 de outubro, está se preparando para um embate com o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), incluindo planos para um impeachment sem precedentes de um de seus ministros, o que poderia ampliar drasticamente o alcance de uma agenda de direita, disseram à Reuters mais de uma dezena de especialistas e funcionários do Senado e do Judiciário. À frente dessa iniciativa estão aliados do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, que dominaram as eleições legislativas deste mês e estão ávidos por vingança contra Alexandre de Moraes, o ministro do Supremo responsável pela prisão e condenação do ex-presidente por conspiração golpista. Isso representaria uma escalada significativa do Poder Legislativo em uma luta de poder que já dura anos com o Judiciário, reafirmando a influência do Congresso e potencialmente empurrando o tribunal para a direita nos próximos anos. Se o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), filho do ex-presidente, derrotar o atual presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, em 25 de outubro, um Judiciário enfraquecido também reduziria um dos principais mecanismos de controle do seu poder. BLOQUEANDO POLÍTICAS DE DIREITA O STF foi o principal obstáculo à agenda de Bolsonaro durante seu mandato na Presidência de 2019 a 2022, bloqueando iniciativas para enfraquecer as proteções ambientais, flexibilizar as restrições da pandemia e facilitar a compra de armas, por exemplo. O Supremo continua a barrar algumas das legislações de direita mais estridentes, definindo efetivamente políticas em assuntos que vão desde os direitos dos povos indígenas até a regulamentação da internet. A eleição deste mês poderá ser crucial, já que o próximo presidente poderá nomear pelo menos quatro dos 11 ministros do Supremo, incluindo uma vaga já existente e substitutos para três ministros que atingirão a idade de aposentadoria compulsória de 75 anos antes do término do próximo mandato presidencial. Após Bolsonaro ter indicado dois ministros para o Supremo, uma vitória de seu filho pode significar uma maioria na corte composta por indicados pela família Bolsonaro até o final de seu mandato, no início de 2031. O impeachment de Moraes, de 57 anos, aceleraria a chegada dessa maioria. "Caso Flávio vença, o próximo governo e o Senado poderão reformular a maioria dos 11 membros do Supremo, o que significa definir, literalmente, o equilíbrio de poder na democracia brasileira por uma geração", disse Bruna Santos, diretora do Programa Brasil do Diálogo Interamericano. CRÍTICAS DE TRUMP E MUSK O processo contra o ex-presidente Bolsonaro, relatado por Moraes, fez dele uma das figuras mais controversas do Brasil, atraindo até mesmo a ira do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, que descreveu o caso como uma "caça às bruxas" e chegou a sancionar o magistrado brevemente em 2025. Moraes também foi alvo de críticas quando ordenou a suspensão do X no Brasil em 2024, após a plataforma desrespeitar ordens judiciais. O proprietário do X, Elon Musk, o acusou de censura e autoritarismo. Apoiadores de Bolsonaro se mobilizam para exigir a destituição do magistrado após um relatório da Polícia Federal revelar comunicações entre Moraes e Daniel Vorcaro, dono do Banco Master preso acusado da maior fraude bancária da história do país. Flávio, que também está sendo investigado por ligações com Vorcaro, também pediu a remoção de Moraes. "Defender o Judiciário significa enfrentar esse problema — abrir um processo de impeachment e dar-lhe o direito à defesa, concluí-lo e virar a página", disse à Reuters o senador eleito Domingos Sávio (PL-MG). Após hesitar num primeiro momento em adotar uma postura mais firme, Lula passou a manifestar publicamente seu apoio à abertura de uma apuração sobre ministros do Supremo, defendendo transparência, divulgação e uma investigação imparcial de todas as suspeitas de corrupção. Nem Moraes nem o Supremo responderam às perguntas da Reuters. O ministro e o restante do tribunal têm defendido suas ações como necessárias para fazer cumprir a lei brasileira e proteger as instituições democráticas. Moraes refere-se às investigações que o envolvem como politicamente e eleitoralmente motivadas, como vingança pela condenação de Bolsonaro, e solicitou uma investigação sobre André Mendonça, ministro do STF que divulgou os relatórios que o implicam. PODER DE FOGO LEGISLATIVO O candidato a vice-presidente de Flávio Bolsonaro, o deputado Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), disse à Reuters que "é preciso rever o que está acontecendo hoje na relação entre o Supremo Tribunal Federal e os demais Poderes, e isso envolve examinar se os ministros cometeram crimes passíveis de impeachment". A Constituição brasileira permite que o Senado julgue ministros do STF por infrações que violem a Constituição. São necessários dois terços dos 81 senadores — ou seja, 54 deles — para condenar e destituir um ministro. Os aliados de Flávio podem já estar próximos desse número quando o próximo Senado tomar posse em fevereiro. Seu partido conquistou um número recorde de 28 cadeiras, e o senador já garantiu o apoio de outros cinco partidos que, juntos, detêm mais 22 cadeiras. Isso elevaria a coligação que o apoia para 50 senadores. Os quatro votos restantes poderiam vir dos 15 senadores de partidos não alinhados. Desde 2023, houve 48 pedidos malsucedidos de impeachment de Moraes no Senado, que nunca chegaram a julgamento porque o presidente do Senado não deu seguimento às denúncias. Isso pode mudar, já que o coordenador de campanha de Flávio, Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), provavelmente se tornará o próximo presidente do Senado. Nos últimos dias, Marinho disse a jornalistas que o Senado não buscará oportunidades para vingança, embora tenha acrescentado que o atual Senado "está falhando em agir" para responsabilizar os ministros do STF. "Se forem cometidos crimes passíveis de impeachment, eles devem ser investigados. Ninguém está acima da lei", disse Marinho. (Reportagem de Ricardo Brito; Reportagem adicional de Brendan O'Boyle)

item.title: South Africa look to re-establish test credentials after Australia mauling
item.description: South Africa will seek to show their heady ascent to the top of the test cricket pile was no accident as they bid to level the series against Australia in the second test, starting on Sunday in Gqeberha.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa will seek to show their heady ascent to the top of the test cricket pile was no accident as they bid to level the series against Australia in the second test, starting on Sunday in Gqeberha. The hosts suffered a [USN:L6N45Z0QL TEXT:"214-run defeat"] to Australia in the first test that ended in Durban on Tuesday, a setback that left their status as world test champions looking increasingly fragile. South Africa secured a [USN:L6N3SH01J TEXT:"dramatic five-wicket victory"] over Australia to win the World Test Championship last year at Lord’s in London, but their qualification for the final prompted debate. They played fewer tests than the likes of England and India and faced what was widely regarded as an easier schedule in the qualifying period. Their winning form leading up to the WTC final also masked some poor batting performances, which coach Shukri Conrad acknowledged finally caught up with them against Australia at Kingsmead, where they looked anything but world champions. “We’ve been heavily reliant on (captain) Temba (Bavuma) and (opener) Aiden Markram and then the lower order runs,” he said after Australia exposed their batting fragility. Several changes are expected for the second test where Matthew Breetzke is set to be given a renewed chance to open alongside Markram. Ryan Rickelton is primed to take over as wicketkeeper from Kyle Verreynne but move down the order. Tristan Stubbs, who batted at number five for the first test, has been omitted, which could open the door for Marques Ackerman to make his test debut. RABADA BACK AFTER LENGTHY ABSENCE South Africa will welcome back paceman Kagiso Rabada for his first outing since the Indian Premier League in May, placing considerable expectation on his shoulders despite his lengthy absence. That means they will drop one spinner. Australia’s selection is also keenly anticipated but with Cameron Green’s return from injury likely delayed, they might resist the temptation to make any changes after such an emphatic win. One possibility, however, is that Scott Boland is brought into the attack as Australia monitor the workloads of Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc after all three bowled at least 29 overs in the first test. Persistent rain and damp conditions are forecast for Gqeberha, particularly on the opening two days, which raises the prospect of delays or a shortened match at St George’s Park.

item.title: China afirma que Israel deve interromper “estabelecimento forçado” de assentamentos na Cisjordânia
item.description: O ministro das Relações Exteriores da China, Wang Yi, disse ao presidente israelense Isaac Herzog que Israel deveria interromper e reverter o “estabelecimento forçado” de assentamentos na Cisjordânia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O ministro das Relações Exteriores da China, Wang Yi, disse ao presidente israelense Isaac Herzog que Israel deveria interromper e reverter o “estabelecimento forçado” de assentamentos na Cisjordânia. A China sempre defendeu que a questão palestina é a maior injustiça histórica deste século, afirmou Wang a Herzog durante uma reunião no Azerbaijão, de acordo com um comunicado divulgado pelo Ministério das Relações Exteriores da China na sexta-feira. Herzog declarou em uma postagem no X que a reunião, realizada na quinta-feira, teve como foco “as relações entre nossos países e a situação no Oriente Médio”. Seu gabinete se recusou a comentar quando questionado sobre as discussões relativas à Cisjordânia ou aos palestinos. Wang afirmou que promover a paz e a reconciliação na região é a “pedra angular” da política da China para o Oriente Médio. A China acredita que a “solução de dois Estados” é o caminho certo para uma resolução e que a prioridade imediata é abrir totalmente o acesso à Faixa de Gaza para que não se permita que uma “catástrofe” humanitária se espalhe, acrescentou Wang. A China está disposta a trabalhar com a comunidade internacional para pressionar todas as partes a retomarem o diálogo e as consultas o mais rápido possível e buscarem uma solução política para o conflito, disse Wang. A China há muito tempo é defensora da causa palestina e também mantém laços estreitos com o principal adversário regional de Israel, o Irã.

item.title: Hedge funds bet Japan reforms have further to run at Sohn Tokyo
item.description: The next phase of Japanese corporate reform took center stage at the Sohn Conference in Tokyo, as hedge fund managers highlighted investment opportunities ranging from a financial conglomerate's capital allocation strategy to an X-ray scattering firm's AI solutions.
item.dc:creator: Summer Zhen, Rocky Swift
item.content:encoded: The next phase of Japanese corporate reform took center stage at the Sohn Conference in Tokyo, as hedge fund managers highlighted investment opportunities ranging from a financial conglomerate's capital allocation strategy to an X-ray scattering firm's AI solutions. At the inaugural Sohn Conference in Japan, which invited 14 funds to pitch their top investment ideas, more than half of the investors favored the theme of corporate reform. Daisuke Nakayama, a portfolio manager at Hong Kong-headquartered Polymer Capital, picked Orix Corporation , a financial services firm, saying the change in management marks "a big turning point" for the company's transformation into a global investment firm. "The new leadership has a greater focus on capital allocation and ROE," Nakayama said, adding the firm is now using overseas capital, including from Qatar Investment Authority, to bid for companies. The number of activist campaigns in Japan hit a record last year, according to brokerage Jefferies, after years of pressure from regulators and the Tokyo Stock Exchange on companies to improve shareholder returns and invest in growth. BEYOND DIVIDENDS AND BUYBACKS Fund managers said that the next chapter is not just about companies increasing dividends and buybacks but also about focusing on those deploying capital to expand businesses and drive long-term growth. One example is Rigaku (268A.T) , an X-ray equipment supplier pivoting to semiconductor metrology, measuring and inspecting chips. New York-based Indus Capital Partners said it had invested in the company and had engaged with the firm to sell a stake to a US semiconductor firm to drive revenue. As semiconductor companies are going into vertical structures to scale, X-ray is needed to detect defects deeper in the 3D chips, said Byron Gill, managing partner at Indus. Rigaku might be one of the few companies that "has the key to unlocking scale for the semiconductor industry in the middle of a super cycle", he added, forecasting a 100% rise in its valuation by 2029. REFORM THEME DOMINATES The corporate reform theme still has a long way to run, market participants said. "Japan changes slowly, but once the change starts, it does not reverse," said Naohide Une, partner and CEO at Investment Lab, a former senior managing director at Japan Post Bank. He picked Japanese chemical company Ube Corporation (4208.T) for its corporate reform efforts. In a separate Q&A session, Seth Fischer, founder of activist Oasis Management, said his fund may substantially increase its stake in Japanese electric motor maker Nidec (6594.T) . AI AS A BACK-OFFICE TAILWIND AI was another key investment theme. Investment firms Ruane Cunniff and Japan Catalyst picked software companies Money Forward (3994.T) and OBIC Business Consultants (4733.T) , respectively. They argued that back-office software operators are AI winners rather than losers, as clients require accuracy. And these businesses are helping Japan overcome labor tightness, they said.

item.title: Poland urges internet firms to act on violent content after school stabbings
item.description: Poland summoned internet companies including Google and Meta to the Digital Affairs Ministry on Friday, demanding they do more to curb the spread of violent content following a series of school stabbing attacks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Poland summoned internet companies including Google (GOOGL.O) and Meta (META.O) to the Digital Affairs Ministry on Friday, demanding they do more to curb the spread of violent content following a series of school stabbing attacks. [USN:L1N45Y0D2 TEXT:"Thousands of police"] were sent to schools this week to ensure security after a series of three attacks in four days triggered a wave of online threats that left pupils and teachers fearing for their safety. Warsaw says the glorification of violence in corners of the internet, for example in groups devoted to Nazi ideology or idolising serial killers, is having a damaging effect on children and has urged social media firms to do more to prevent content that encourages or threatens violence. "It is the expectation of every Polish citizen that ... no one should incite others to commit suicide, that there should be no content endorsing or encouraging criminal threats, and that users should not be exposed to situations like acts of murder, physical harm, or mutilation," Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski told a press conference. Gawkowski said that between October 7 and October 12 Poland flagged 89 cases of illegal content related to the attacks to internet companies, and in two-thirds of cases they failed to take any action. The meeting was attended by representatives of Google, Meta, TikTok, Discord and Telegram. Elon Musk's X was invited but did not attend, Gawkowski said. The companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The government is fast-tracking legislation to make it easier and quicker to remove damaging content. The latest stabbing occurred on Saturday, when three people were injured at a further education college in Warsaw. It followed an attack on October 8 in Leszczydol-Nowiny, northeast of the capital, where a 15-year-old former pupil wearing a helmet-mounted camera [USN:L8N45U0GO TEXT:"killed a school caretaker"] and wounded two teachers. A day earlier, a 19-year-old [USN:L1N45T0N9 TEXT:"injured 10 people"], including himself, at a school in Ostroleka.

item.title: US equity funds draw renewed inflows as Treasury yields ease
item.description: US equity funds attracted inflows in the week to October 14, following outflows the previous week, as Treasury yields eased from recent peaks and investors looked ahead to a strong earnings season, although the technology sector faced outflows amid concerns over rising debt levels.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US equity funds attracted inflows in the week to October 14, following outflows the previous week, as Treasury yields eased from recent peaks and investors looked ahead to a strong earnings season, although the technology sector faced outflows amid concerns over rising [USN:L6N4610C5 TEXT:"debt"] levels. Investors purchased a net $13.01 billion in US equity funds during the week, reversing net outflows of $5.1 billion in the previous week, according to LSEG Lipper data. The technology sector, meanwhile, recorded net outflows of $5.21 billion, its largest weekly outflow since June 24. The US 10-year Treasury yield fell about 26 basis points from the 24½-year high of 5.3645% reached the previous week, amid expectations that the Federal Reserve may [USN:L6N4601E8 TEXT:"hold"] interest rates steady at its meeting this month. Investors also drew confidence from strong corporate earnings expectations in the ongoing earnings season. LSEG data, based on analyst estimates for 2,076 US large- and mid-cap companies, forecasts year-on-year profit growth of 29.99% for the most recent quarter, with the technology sector expected to post growth of 57.64%. US large-cap equity funds attracted $16.55 billion, reversing roughly $14.08 billion in outflows the previous week. Investors also bought $2.12 billion in multi-cap funds and $541 million in small-cap funds, while selling a net $651 million in mid-cap funds. US bond funds remained popular for a 26th consecutive week, attracting net inflows of $6.45 billion. General domestic taxable fixed-income funds recorded $1.91 billion in net inflows, marking a fourth straight week of net purchases. Investors also added $1.61 billion to municipal debt funds and $1.12 billion to short- and intermediate-term government and Treasury funds. Meanwhile, investors withdrew $45.93 billion from money market funds, following $68.49 billion in net purchases the previous week.

item.title: Spain punished by FIFA for Islamophobic chants in Egypt friendly
item.description: Spain have been fined $20,000 and ordered to partially close their stadium for their next friendly after supporters chanted Islamophobic slogans twice during a game against Egypt in March, FIFA said in a statement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spain have been fined $20,000 and ordered to partially close their stadium for their next friendly after supporters chanted Islamophobic slogans twice during a game against Egypt in March, FIFA said in a statement. The sanctions relate to incidents at the RCDE Stadium near Barcelona, home of LaLiga club Espanyol, where some Spain fans chanted, "Who doesn't jump is a Muslim" during a World Cup warm-up match which ended in a 0-0 draw. After the second occurrence of the chant, the stadium announcer issued a warning and the scoreboard displayed a message against discriminatory behaviour. Spain winger Lamine Yamal, who is Muslim, condemned the chants at the time, describing them as disrespectful and intolerable and calling those responsible "ignorant and racist". Spanish [USN:L1N40K0IS TEXT:"police launched an investigation"] the following day while world governing body FIFA later [USN:L4N40Q1AO TEXT:"started disciplinary proceedings"] against the Spanish soccer federation (RFEF). The RFEF argued that the word 'Muslim' was "neither insulting nor pejorative", adding the fans' conduct should be assessed under FIFA's Article 17, which covers political, ideological, religious or offensive messages, rather than Article 15, which deals with discrimination and racist abuse. However, FIFA's disciplinary committee rejected that argument, saying Article 15 does not require the explicit use of a slur and that a term can be discriminatory when used in context as "an insult, taunt, or marker of inferiority". FIFA fined the RFEF and ordered the closure of at least 15% of available seats for Spain's next friendly. Reuters has contacted the RFEF for comment.

item.title: Brazil economic activity up 0.3% in August, matching forecasts
item.description: Economic activity in Brazil rose by a seasonally adjusted 0.3% in August from the previous month, a central bank index showed on Friday, matching the median forecast in a Reuters poll of economists.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Economic activity in Brazil rose by a seasonally adjusted 0.3% in August from the previous month, a central bank index showed on Friday, matching the median forecast in a Reuters poll of economists. The IBC-Br index, a proxy for gross domestic product, is compiled using the bank's estimates for agriculture, industry and services, as well as taxes linked to production August's gain was driven by industry, which expanded 0.9% from July On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 1.2% from a year earlier and rose 1.6% on a rolling 12-month basis through August Brazil's central bank has [USN:L1N45G0PM TEXT:"argued"] that slower economic activity is needed for inflation to converge to its 3% target The bank [USN:L1N45G0CQ TEXT:"forecasts"] gross domestic product growth of 1.8% this year, slowing to 1.4% in 2027 Policymakers are due to meet in early November for their next monetary policy decision after delivering five straight 25-basis-point interest rate cuts, bringing the benchmark Selic rate to 13.75%

item.title: Papa Leão fará aparição no domingo após "melhora constante", diz Vaticano
item.description: O papa Leão vem apresentando uma melhora constante no hospital após ter sido submetido a uma cirurgia para câncer de pulmão na terça-feira, informou o Vaticano, acrescentando que ele já consegue realizar suas atividades diárias normais com total autonomia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O papa Leão vem apresentando uma melhora constante no hospital após ter sido submetido a uma cirurgia para câncer de pulmão na terça-feira, informou o Vaticano, acrescentando que ele já consegue realizar suas atividades diárias normais com total autonomia. O papa fará no domingo sua primeira aparição pública desde a internação para conduzir a tradicional oração do Angelus, enquanto continuam os preparativos para sua viagem à América do Sul, prevista para novembro, segundo o Vaticano. Leão foi diagnosticado com adenocarcinoma pulmonar, a forma mais comum de câncer de pulmão, e os médicos removeram o lobo inferior de seu pulmão direito em uma cirurgia realizada na terça-feira. O Vaticano divulgou, nesta sexta-feira, as primeiras imagens do papa desde a cirurgia, mostrando-o celebrando missa e de pé, sem precisar de auxílio. "No momento, não recebemos nenhuma comunicação dos médicos sobre a sua alta, além do que nos foi dito desde o início, sobre um prazo de uma semana", afirmou um porta-voz do Vaticano. Leão, de 71 anos, tem uma viagem programada para Uruguai, Argentina e Peru, entre os dias 6 e 17 de novembro. A presidente peruana, Keiko Fujimori, havia aventado a possibilidade de a viagem precisar ser adiada, mas em um sinal de que os preparativos seguem seu curso normal, o Vaticano divulgou uma lista de jornalistas credenciados para cobrir a visita. Os preparativos para a viagem "seguem avançando", disse o porta-voz do Vaticano.

item.title: Russian strikes and winter hardship may drive more Ukrainians from homes, UN agency warns
item.description: Millions of Ukrainians face another winter of hardship as attacks on critical infrastructure, damaged housing and rising living costs threaten to force more people from their homes, the United Nations migration agency said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Millions of Ukrainians face another winter of hardship as attacks on critical infrastructure, damaged housing and rising living costs threaten to force more people from their homes, the United Nations migration agency said on Friday. With temperatures set to fall in the coming months, many families are struggling to secure reliable heating, electricity and water after years of war, the International Organization for Migration said. This week, Russian missiles and drones have [USN:L1N46209U TEXT:"rained down on Ukrainian cities"], amid fears that the US could pull back intelligence sharing and weapons support from Kyiv. "Winter is fast approaching in Ukraine, and for many Ukrainians, the months ahead could be the most difficult since the full-scale war began," Dejan Keserovic, IOM deputy chief of mission in Ukraine, told reporters in Geneva via video link from Kyiv. Nearly 3.6 million people remain internally displaced across Ukraine since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, while an estimated 3.8 million have returned after displacement, often to damaged or partially destroyed homes, according to the latest IOM figures. Ukrainians who returned to their homes within the last three months are the most likely to say they intend to leave again, reflecting growing concerns about deteriorating living conditions, the IOM said. European countries such as Poland, Germany and the Czech Republic currently host around 6 million Ukrainian refugees. Keserovic said he expected host countries to be preparing for more Ukrainians to leave if the situation got worse. Repeated Russian strikes on energy and other critical infrastructure have put increasing pressure on Ukraine's electricity, heating and water systems, while drone and missile attacks continue to kill and injure civilians across the country, the IOM said. Reliable access to water is emerging as a major concern because water systems depend heavily on electricity, the IOM said. The UN agency has installed 31 solar power stations to support water systems across Ukraine, but warned that needs remain immense. The IOM also warned that funding shortages could hamper aid efforts, with less than 7% of its 2026 Ukraine response plan funded so far, and said urgent resources were needed to improve insulation as households face freezing conditions.

item.title: El papa muestra una "mejoría constante" tras una cirugía por cáncer de pulmón, dice el Vaticano
item.description: El papa León muestra una mejoría constante en el hospital tras someterse el martes a una cirugía por cáncer de pulmón, informó el Vaticano, que añadió que el pontífice ya puede realizar sus actividades cotidianas habituales con plena autonomía.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El papa León muestra una mejoría constante en el hospital tras someterse el martes a una cirugía por cáncer de pulmón, informó el Vaticano, que añadió que el pontífice ya puede realizar sus actividades cotidianas habituales con plena autonomía. El papa hará el domingo su primera aparición pública desde su hospitalización para rezar el tradicional Ángelus, mientras continúan los preparativos de su viaje previsto a Sudamérica en noviembre, indicó el Vaticano.

item.title: Naftogaz-Chef: Ukraine mit größten Gasreserven seit sechs Jahren
item.description: Die Ukraine hat trotz verstärkter russischer Angriffe auf ihre Energieinfrastruktur die größten Gasreserven seit sechs Jahren für den Winter aufgebaut. Der staatliche Energiekonzern Naftogaz habe die Vorräte in den unterirdischen Speichern auf 16 Milliarden Kubikmeter erhöht, sagte der kommissarische Konzernchef Serhij Fedorenko in einem am Freitag veröffentlichten Interview der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Dies ist der höchste Stand seit 2020. Im vergangenen Jahr war das Land mit weniger als 14 Milliarden Kubikmetern in die Heizperiode gestartet.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Polityuk
item.content:encoded: Die Ukraine hat trotz verstärkter russischer Angriffe auf ihre Energieinfrastruktur die größten Gasreserven seit sechs Jahren für den Winter aufgebaut. Der staatliche Energiekonzern Naftogaz habe die Vorräte in den unterirdischen Speichern auf 16 Milliarden Kubikmeter erhöht, sagte der kommissarische Konzernchef Serhij Fedorenko in einem am Freitag veröffentlichten Interview der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Dies ist der höchste Stand seit 2020. Im vergangenen Jahr war das Land mit weniger als 14 Milliarden Kubikmetern in die Heizperiode gestartet. Die Regierung in Kiew hatte als Mindestziel für diesen Winter 13,2 Milliarden Kubikmeter vorgegeben. Der bevorstehende Winter könnte der schwierigste in dem nunmehr fast fünf Jahre andauernden Krieg mit Russland werden. Die russischen Streitkräfte haben ihre Angriffe auf den ukrainischen Energiesektor zuletzt deutlich verschärft. Laut Fedorenko wurden Anlagen des Konzerns in diesem Jahr mehr als 400 Mal unter Beschuss genommen – doppelt so oft wie 2025. "In diesem Jahr wurden die meisten unserer Anlagen angegriffen", sagte er. Betroffen seien die Förderung, Verarbeitung und der Transport von Öl und Gas sowie Wärmekraftwerke in den frontnahen Regionen. "Wir verstärken die Verteidigung und graben uns ein", sagte Fedorenko. "Wir blicken vorsichtig nach vorn. Jeden Morgen wache ich auf und schaue auf mein Handy, um zu sehen, ob in der Nacht eine unserer Anlagen getroffen wurde." Dennoch werde die zerstörte Infrastruktur kontinuierlich wieder aufgebaut. FRÜHZEITIGE LIEFERUNGEN Der Anstieg der Reserven ist zudem auf einen sinkenden Verbrauch zurückzuführen, da russische Angriffe auf Industrieanlagen die Schließung einiger Fabriken zur Folge hatten. Fedorenko schätzt, dass der Gasverbrauch im Jahr 2026 auf rund 20 Milliarden Kubikmeter sinken wird, nach 21 Milliarden Kubikmetern im Vorjahr. Die Ukraine deckt ihren Bedarf teilweise durch Importe. Seit 2015 kauft das Land kein Gas mehr direkt aus Russland, sondern importiert es von europäischen Lieferanten über Polen, die Slowakei und Ungarn. Starker Frost und russische Angriffe auf Speicher erforderten im Jahr 2025 und im ersten Quartal 2026 Rekordimporte von 7,8 Milliarden Kubikmetern. Für die laufende Saison habe Naftogaz frühzeitig Lieferungen von mehr als einer Milliarde Kubikmetern vertraglich gesichert, wovon ein Viertel auf Flüssigerdgas (LNG) entfalle. "Wir haben Lieferungen speziell für die Heizperiode vereinbart. Das bedeutet, dass wir Lieferverträge für den Zeitraum von Dezember bis März abgeschlossen haben", sagte Fedorenko. Die Ukraine verfügt über die größten unterirdischen Gasspeicher Europas mit einer Kapazität von rund 30 Milliarden Kubikmetern. Fedorenko zufolge hat Kiew der Europäischen Union angeboten, ein Drittel dieser Kapazität für europäische Gasreserven zu nutzen. Da die Speicher mehr als einen Kilometer unter der Erde lägen, seien sie vor Angriffen geschützt. Zudem könne das Gas bei Bedarf sehr schnell an Verbraucher vor allem in Osteuropa geliefert werden. Die ukrainischen Tarife für die Gasspeicherung seien derzeit die niedrigsten in der EU. Nach ukrainischem Recht ist es staatlichen Unternehmen untersagt, Daten über die Betriebsergebnisse im Energiesektor zu veröffentlichen.

item.title: Índice de atividade econômica do Banco Central tem alta de 0,30% em agosto, em linha com o esperado
item.description: O Índice de Atividade Econômica do Banco Central (IBC-Br) apontou crescimento de 0,30% em agosto sobre julho, informou a autarquia nesta sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Índice de Atividade Econômica do Banco Central (IBC-Br) apontou crescimento de 0,30% em agosto sobre julho, informou a autarquia nesta sexta-feira. O dado veio exatamente em linha com o esperado por economistas, segundo pesquisa da Reuters. (BRIBC=ECI) Na comparação com agosto do ano passado, o IBC-Br teve ganho de 1,2%, e em 12 meses acumulou alta de 1,6%.

item.title: Pope Leo to make Sunday appearance after 'steady improvement' from cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo will appear in public on Sunday for the first time since undergoing lung cancer surgery as the 71-year-old pontiff shows steady improvement and is able to work and do normal daily activities independently, the Vatican said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: Pope Leo will appear in public on Sunday for the first time since undergoing lung cancer surgery as the 71-year-old pontiff shows steady improvement and is able to work and do normal daily activities independently, the Vatican said on Friday. Leo will be seen leading a traditional noontime prayer on Sunday, the Vatican said, while preparations continue for his planned November trip to South America. The pope was diagnosed with [USN:L8N46006S TEXT:"lung adenocarcinoma"], the most common form of lung cancer, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung in an operation on Tuesday. The Vatican on Friday released the first images of the pope since his surgery, showing him celebrating Mass and standing unaided. Leo underwent blood tests and a chest X-ray this morning, "confirming steady improvement in his overall condition", according to the latest medical bulletin on his condition. "His post-operative recovery is allowing him to carry out normal daily activities with full independence," it said. SOUTH AMERICA TRIP 'GOING FORWARD' The cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be relatively young and energetic and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the [USN:L8N4600P9 TEXT:"future shape of his papacy"] as he deals with the illness. The Vatican signaled on Friday that Leo, known for keeping a busy schedule, intended to keep up his commitments, as some cardinals began to publicly express concern about the pope's health. The Vatican said work on his November 6 to 17 visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru was "going forward" and released a list of journalists accredited to travel with Leo and cover the trip. Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori had speculated previously that the trip might have to be delayed. Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican's secretary of state, said on Friday it was unclear when Leo would be able to return to his usual rhythm of appointments. "The question now is when he will return, under what circumstances he will return, and what the doctors say," he said on the sidelines of an event in Rome, according to Italian agencies. CARDINAL SHOCKED AT CANCER DIAGNOSIS The Vatican did not say on Friday when the pope might be discharged from hospital. It has previously indicated his recovery would take about a week. The pope's doctors have said his surgery was completed successfully, without complications. They have not yet disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis. Chicago Cardinal Blase Cupich, seen as a close ally of Leo, said he had been shocked by news of the cancer diagnosis. He told Catholic magazine America he thought Leo had "downplayed" his health issue on Sunday, when the pope [USN:L1N45X029 TEXT:"announced"] he needed surgery for a small, well-contained growth on his lung. "When I heard they took out part of the lobe of the lung and that it was malignant, that was more shocking and more concerning," said Cupich. "I think people are very concerned and even worried about this but hoping for the best."

item.title: ExxonMobil signals $4.5 billion refining earnings boost as margins soar
item.description: ExxonMobil signaled on Friday that higher refining margins during the third quarter could boost its downstream profit by $4.5 billion compared with the previous three months.
item.dc:creator: Sheila Dang
item.content:encoded: ExxonMobil (XOM.N) signaled on Friday that higher refining margins during the third quarter could boost its downstream profit by $4.5 billion compared with the previous three months. Refining margins have soared due to the ongoing Iran war , which has restricted energy exports through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as Ukrainian attacks on [USN:L1N46203J TEXT:"Russian refineries"]. The resulting higher fuel prices have created political risks for the administration of US President Donald Trump ahead of the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"] in November. The top US oil producer's expected refining boom could further draw [USN:L1N4400L8 TEXT:"the ire of the president"], who complained in August that Exxon and Chevron (CVX.N) were making "too much money". Exxon's regulatory filing indicates that adjusted net income for the refining business could jump to $8.5 billion, wrote BMO Capital Markets analyst Phillip Jungwirth in a research note. That would be more than double last quarter's profit level. Here are more details from Exxon's earnings preview: Upstream earnings could take a $1.3 billion hit compared with the second quarter. The average closing Brent benchmark price declined about 5.6% during the third quarter compared with the previous three months, according to LSEG data. Exxon indicated that there were no volume-related disruptions during the quarter stemming from the Iran war. The company's move to divest some upstream assets will boost earnings by $700 million. Exxon will release full third-quarter results on October 30. Exxon shares were up less than 1% in pre-market trading.

item.title: Why is the battle for Yemen's Taiz so important?
item.description: The city of Taiz is rapidly emerging as the most important battlefront in Yemen's reignited civil war, pitting the Iran-allied Houthis against the internationally recognised government, which is backed by a Saudi-led coalition.
item.dc:creator: Angus Mcdowall
item.content:encoded: The city of Taiz is rapidly emerging as the most important battlefront in Yemen's [USN:L6N45S0PX TEXT:"reignited civil war"], pitting the Iran-allied [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"Houthis"] against the internationally recognised government, which is backed by a Saudi-led coalition. Houthi forces have [USN:L1N45Z0S1 TEXT:"encircled Taiz"] in recent weeks by cutting its main road south to Aden, causing widespread displacement and worsening a humanitarian crisis. Here's what you need to know: WHY IS TAIZ SO IMPORTANT? Any Houthi victory in Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, would mark one of the biggest turning points in the country's long civil war, which resumed this summer after a four-year truce. Taiz city has an estimated population of almost 600,000, said Katja Juric, Aden-based head of programmes for the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Government sources said 80,000 had fled in the latest fighting. Taiz has been on the frontline between the Houthis and the government since the first days of the conflict that started in early 2015 and has long been seen as a bastion of opposition to the Iran-allied group. It is the last major urban stronghold of anti-Houthi forces in the southern highland area of Yemen: the rugged hills above both Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based, and the flat coastal plain around the [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb"] Strait. A Houthi takeover of Taiz would make it much harder for government forces to maintain their counterattack around Bab el-Mandeb and keep the Houthis at arm's length from Aden. It would also mean a resounding symbolic defeat for the government and the military coalition of Saudi-backed Yemeni forces fighting the Houthis. WHAT'S THE MILITARY SITUATION AROUND TAIZ? For years the city has sat at the tip of a government salient stretching north into Houthi territory. The Houthis held areas to the north, east and west of Taiz, while government forces had the city and its immediate surroundings including Jebel Sabar, the high mountain rising above it to the south. As fighting in Yemen resumed in recent weeks, the Houthis began making advances to cut off Taiz by seizing territory to the south of Jebel Sabar along the road to Aden, which snakes about 200 km (125 miles) through rugged hills where fighting is slow and difficult. Sections of the road are now under Houthi control, including at the towns of al-Turbah and Mudiriyat al-Misrakh, leaving Taiz encircled since early October, with the Houthis sometimes shelling government positions in and around the city. Government forces, backed by airstrikes from the Saudi-led coalition, are trying to drive the Houthis back from their recent gains and reopen the road, but were still losing ground around Taiz rather than recapturing territory in mid-October. WHY IS TAIZ A STRONGHOLD OF OPPOSITION TO THE HOUTHIS? Taiz had a long history of difficult ties with rulers from north Yemen and was a hotbed of the 2011 Arab Spring uprisings that toppled veteran former president Ali Abdullah Saleh. While the Houthis adhere to the Zaydi school of Shi'ite Islam, Taiz is predominantly Sunni Muslim. Saleh and the Houthis joined forces to seize the capital, Sanaa, in 2014, derailing a political transition that arose out of the Arab Spring and had led to a proposal for a federal, democratic state. In early 2015, army units loyal to Saleh seized positions in the city, leading to big protests there followed by armed clashes. Protesters accused Saleh and the Houthis of mounting a coup d'etat. Months of fierce fighting in and around the city followed, with the Houthis and Saleh's army units battling local fighters and army brigades from Yemen's now fragmented military that backed the government. Taiz citizens endured shelling, sniper fire and terrible shortages in a long siege before government forces eventually drove the Houthis and their allies from the city and re-established a land route to Aden. The fighting in the city lasted throughout 2015 and parts of 2016, and the siege ran for long stretches until 2017. WHAT IS THE HUMANITARIAN SITUATION IN TAIZ? The latest fighting has displaced at least 121,000 in Taiz province, according to the IOM, though many of these are from rural areas outside the city. Inside Taiz, residents have told Reuters about the shortages they now face of basic items and the huge increase in prices they see in the city markets since the Houthis cut the road to Aden. Aid agencies have reported widespread shortages of fuel, food, medicines and clean water. Wheat flour stocks in the city are nearly exhausted, the World Food Programme said in mid-October. The situation risks worsening existing health problems. The UN children's agency UNICEF recently found that one in three of the children it screened in Yemen was malnourished. Cholera, dengue and malaria are all present in Yemen too. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT? Government forces backed by Saudi airstrikes are still trying to take back territory to reopen the road, but there is no guarantee they will succeed. The Houthis, who have [USN:L1N46209G TEXT:"upped their attacks"] on Saudi targets while showing themselves [USN:L6N4580DE TEXT:"better armed"] and organised than in earlier phases of the war, are meanwhile trying to cement their siege of Taiz and move closer towards the city. That might lead to a prolonged siege of the kind that Taiz experienced in the earlier phase of the war. It's also possible the Houthis might try to take the city. Local opposition means resistance could be fierce and any such attempt could cause a long, bloody battle.

Russia seizes more EU companies’ assets over Ukraine support

Reuters

16 October, 2026 05:30 pm IST

By Gleb Bryanski MOSCOW, Oct 16 (Reuters) – Russia has seized local assets of four companies from France, Germany, Sweden and Belgium, according to a decree by President Vladimir Putin, in retaliation for Europe’s wartime support for Ukraine.

Thursday’s decree listed assets belonging to French flooring maker Tarkett, German packaging maker Menshen, Swedish packaging maker Sverige International Holdings and Belgian hygiene product company Ontex.

The decree also listed Russian assets of former European metal-packaging business Eviosys acquired by US packaging group Sonoco in December 2024. The decree listed the assets as owned by Sonoco’s Dutch unit.

Show Full Article

EU leaders rallied around President Volodymyr Zelenskiy at a summit on Friday at one of the most difficult moments for Ukraine amid fears that the US could pull back intelligence sharing and weapons support from Kyiv.

The Kremlin said that the assets’ takeover continued a trend after a similar move last month against food giant Nestle and retailers Auchan and Metro.

“Their country of origin was one of the factors taken into account in making the decision,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said, adding that these countries were involved in “illegal expropriations of Russian property.”

Temporary administration of the European companies’ properties was handed to Russian companies that had been largely unknown.

PUTIN NOTES ‘DOWNSIDES’

Ontex, which employs 350 people in Russia and operates a factory outside Moscow, said it has been informed about the decree and will “consider appropriate actions to safeguard its assets and the continuity of Ontex Russia’s operations.”

Sonoco said in its 2025 report that it had finalised its own exit from Russia in 2022 but acquired more assets, making up 0.5% of the company’s total, as part of the Eviosys deal.

Tarkett said it was “losing effective control over its operations in Russia” and was assessing the situation.

The Kremlin said the measures responded to EU nations’ involvement in “direct battlefield hostilities” but were also “reversible.”

Speaking to Russian businessmen just before the decree was published on Thursday, Putin acknowledged that taking Western assets had “certain downsides” without giving more details.

He urged the Russian businesses taking over the assets to seek domestic financing sources instead.

Putin cited the 2008 global financial crisis, which had a profound impact on the Russian economy, as an example of the risks of excessive exposure to global markets. He said foreign countries pursued their own interests through investment.

There have been some reports that the US could seek control of some Russian assets frozen in Europe as part of efforts to provide incentives for Russia to negotiate with Ukraine.

Russia criticises the EU for freezing about €210 billion ($238 billion) of its sovereign assets in response to the war and for targeting assets belonging to Russian companies in Europe and other Western countries.

(Reporting by Gleb Byranksi in Moscow; Additional reporting by Elena Fabrichnaya, Gleb Stolyarov in Moscow and Mateusz Rabiega in Gdansk; Editing by Edwina Gibbs and Andrew Cawthorne)

item.title: 欧州、債務持続性へ成長加速と赤字削減を＝ＩＭＦ
item.description:
Jan Strupczewski
［バンコク １６日 ロイター］ - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１６日、欧州各国が公的債...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州、債務持続性へ成長加速と赤字削減を＝ＩＭＦ 20:59 配信

国際通貨基金（IMF）のロゴ、ワシントンの本部で2024年撮影 REUTERS/Benoit Tessier/File Photo

Jan Strupczewski

［バンコク　１６日　ロイター］ - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１６日、欧州各国が公的債務を持続可能な水準に維持するには成長を加速させるか、借り入れを減らす必要があるとし、「何もしないという選択肢はない」と警告した。

ＩＭＦは１３日、ユーロ圏の経済成長率について、４月時点と同じく２０２６年が１．１％、２７年は１．２％と予想した。インフレ率は、２６年が３．１％、２７年が２．８％、２８年が２．２％になると予測した。

ＩＭＦは「債務の持続可能性を保つには、欧州諸国の約４分の３で、成長を高めて歳出圧力を緩和する構造改革と、中期的に国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比で平均約３．５％に相当する財政赤字削減策を組み合わせる必要がある」と指摘した。

欧州連合（ＥＵ）全加盟国が欧州委員会と合意しなければならない「中期財政・構造計画」で予定されている財政再建規模はＧＤＰ比で平均約２％にとどまり、一部の国で必要とされる水準を下回っているという。

「スタッフの基本予測は、大半の国で財政再建が計画を下回ることを示しており、想定されている再建規模でさえ達成が困難となる恐れがある」と指摘。

「欧州諸国の約４分の１は、公的債務を持続可能にするためにＧＤＰ比で５％超の財政再建が必要となる。これは過去に実行可能と証明された水準を上回っており、政府活動の範囲を見直し、不足分を補うために民間部門の役割を拡大する以外に選択肢はない」と分析した。

欧州委が５月に発表した予測によると、ＥＵ全体の債務の対ＧＤＰ比率は、２５年末時点の８２．８％から２６年に８４．２％、２７年末までには８５．３％へ上昇する見通し。ユーロ圏の比率も２５年の８８．７％から２６年に９０．２％に上昇し、２７年には９１．２％に達すると予測されている。

ＩＭＦ欧州局長のマテウシュ・シュチュレク氏はロイターに対し、「高齢化、国防費増額、エネルギー移行など、欧州の大半の国が直面している長期的な歳出課題を勘案すると、政策変更がなければ欧州の平均的な経済において公的債務は大幅に増加し、現在の水準の最大２倍に達する可能性がある」と述べ、中欧の高成長国の一部では、この債務拡大のペースがさらに速くなる可能性があるとした。

「持続可能性の定義が（債務の）増大を止めて安定化させられるかどうかであるなら、財政面での対応と再建が不可欠だ」とし、「より早く動く方が常に対処費用は少なくて済む。着手が遅れるほど調整は難しくなる」と語った。

ＩＭＦは欧州の成長加速に向けた最大の障害は低水準の生産性だと指摘し、各国政府に対してＥＵ域内市場の障壁を取り除き、技術革新（イノベーション）や事業拡大への投資を行うよう求めた。

「一定の改革に向けた取り組みが進められているものの、未完成のＥＵ単一市場と各国の障壁が、企業の事業調整や規模拡大、より大きな市場へのアクセスを困難にしている」とした。

また、化石燃料から再生可能エネルギーへの移行を継続し、重要鉱物を含む世界的なサプライチェーン（供給網）の多様化を進めるよう呼びかけた。これらは全てＥＵが既に取り組んでいる政策方針となる。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：年初来安値で確認する円の「現在地」、円安は欧州通貨高の裏返し＝唐鎌大輔氏 コラム：短距離フライト削減でＣＯ2対策なるか、的外れの欧州 焦点：コーヒー企業「アフリカ離れ」も、ＥＵが森林破壊防止法 アングル：欧州熱波、マクロ経済面からの市場注目ポイント コラム：米だけ「異世界」のＩＭＦ会合　イラン戦争無視で政権の苦境露呈 最終更新: 10/16(金) 20:59 ロイター

item.title: Candidate party affiliation will appear on Georgia midterm ballots
item.description: A Georgia law making some county-level elections nonpartisan from 2028 will not affect the November midterm election or remove candidate party labels from any statewide or national ballots as suggested in misleading social media posts.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: A Georgia law making some county-level elections nonpartisan from 2028 will not affect the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"November midterm election"] or remove candidate party labels from any statewide or national ballots as suggested in misleading social media posts. An October 4 Facebook post addressed to "Georgia voters" said the State Election Board of Georgia "has decided to remove the (R) and the (D) that normally appears next to candidate’s names on the upcoming midterms ballots." However, the post is referring to legislation that is not yet in force and affects only local elections in five counties in the greater Atlanta area. Georgia House Bill 369 , which Governor Brian Kemp signed on May 12, calls for nonpartisan races for the district attorney and nearly all offices in those counties, such as tax commissioner and certain court clerks, starting on January 1, 2028. The law won’t affect the November ballots, a spokesperson for the Office of the Georgia Secretary of State said in an emailed statement. "Voters will clearly see partisan affiliation when they cast their ballots, period." A current sample ballot on the official website of Fulton County, one of the five counties where Georgia House Bill 369 will apply, shows partisan affiliations next to candidate names for the upcoming midterm. VERDICT Misleading. While Georgia plans to shift to nonpartisan elections for local offices in some counties, the legislation is not yet in effect and will not eliminate party affiliation from the November 3 midterm ballot or other statewide and national election ballots. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more about our fact-checking work.

item.title: Shell agrees proposed sale of French fuel stations to DCC Energy, source says
item.description: Shell has agreed a deal with Dublin-based DCC Energy for the proposed sale of its network of fuel retail stations and related transport-fuels services in France, according to a person familiar with the matter and documents seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Kelly, Dimitri Rhodes
item.content:encoded: Shell (SHEL.L) has agreed a deal with Dublin-based DCC Energy for the proposed sale of its network of fuel retail stations and related transport-fuels services in France, according to a person familiar with the matter and documents seen by Reuters. The agreement comes as Shell aims to focus its fuel retail and charging operations on key markets where it generates the majority of its cash flow, including the US, Canada and the United Kingdom. The parties have yet to finalise the deal, although completion is expected in the second quarter of 2027, subject to consultation with employee representatives, the document showed. The transaction would include around 70 sites, eight LNG installations and the transfer of 35 employees, the document showed. "Shell is considering a sale of its retail forecourts business in France," Shell told Reuters, adding that it would not comment further at this stage. DCC Energy, a sales and distribution company in Europe and the US, serves millions of customers across the industrial and public sectors and delivers off-grid energy solutions, led by liquid gas, the company's website said. It also operates service stations and fleet services. DCC Energy would operate the stations under a long-term Shell brand licence, the document showed. However, Shell's core fuel supply operations are excluded, meaning the buyer would source its fuel independently. The monetary value of the deal could not immediately be determined. Shell's marketing unit, which includes its fuel and charging retail stations, reported $1.3 billion in adjusted earnings in the second quarter this year, compared with $1.2 billion during the same time last year.

item.title: 仏借り入れコスト上昇、長期化なら財政健全化圧力高まる＝ＩＭＦ
item.description:
Jan Strupczewski
[バンコク １６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のシュチュレク欧州局長はフ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
仏借り入れコスト上昇、長期化なら財政健全化圧力高まる＝ＩＭＦ 20:55 配信

シュチュレクＩＭＦ欧州局長、１４日撮影 REUTERS/Patipat Janthong

Jan Strupczewski

[バンコク １６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のシュチュレク欧州局長はフランスの借り入れコストが上がっていることについて、短期的には対処できるとの見方を示した。ただ上昇が続けば２０２７年予算だけでなく、信頼性のある中期的な財政健全化計画の策定を求める圧力が強まると指摘した。

シュチュレク氏はバンコクで開かれているＩＭＦ年次総会の合間にロイターの取材に応じた。現時点では仏国債市場はまだ秩序立った動きを保っているとの認識を示した。

「（市場には）流動性があり、（国債の）償還期間もかなり長く、投資家層も多様だ。銀行の流動性が高いことも支えになっている。このため短期的な債務リスクには十分対応できる」と語った。

一方、「利回りの高止まりが長引けば、財政とコスト抑制への圧力が強まる。財政の不均衡是正が急務であることを改めて認識させる。まずは２７年予算から着手すべきで、欧州連合（ＥＵ）の財政ルールに沿って遅滞なく承認される必要がある」と述べた。

フランスは２６年の財政赤字を国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比５．４％と見込む。２７年は５．０％への引き下げを目標としている。ＥＵの法令を順守するには、２９年までに赤字をＧＤＰ比３％未満に抑える必要がある。

シュチュレク氏は「それは確かに必要だ。市場の動きは、われわれにもフランスの政策当局者にも、その必要性を改めて認識させている」とし「市場のシグナルには政策を変える力がある。過去に何度も見てきた。ある意味では、債券市場から現実を突き付けられることで、財政調整のあり方が変わり、調整が加速する可能性がある」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：米国債の「ベーシス取引」、軟着陸は可能か コラム：米財務省の借入拡大、債務問題の大きさに比べれば単なるノイズ 焦点：仏、財政赤字巡り政局緊迫　大統領選控え市場の不安と格下げ警戒 コラム：米だけ「異世界」のＩＭＦ会合　イラン戦争無視で政権の苦境露呈 最終更新: 10/16(金) 20:55 ロイター

item.description: Oct 16 : Michael Saylor's Strategy faces potential removal from MSCI's global equity indexes under new rules adopted on Thursday, threatening billions of dollars in passive investment in the bitcoin buyer.Shares of Strategy, the world's biggest corporate bitcoin holder and a constituent of the MSCI USA and MS
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Business

Strategy faces MSCI ouster under new rules, billions in passive holdings at risk

FILE PHOTO: Michael Saylor, Chairman of the Board of Directors and Chief Executive Office of MicroStrategy Inc, speaks during the Bitcoin Conference 2023, in Miami Beach, Florida, U.S., May 19, 2023. REUTERS/Marco Bello/File Photo

FAST

Oct 16 : Michael Saylor's Strategy faces potential removal from MSCI's global equity indexes under new rules adopted on Thursday, threatening billions of dollars in passive investment in the bitcoin buyer. Shares of Strategy, the world's biggest corporate bitcoin holder and a constituent of the MSCI USA and MSCI World indexes, fell 2.7 per cent in premarket trading on Friday. MSCI said on Thursday non-operating companies will be ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes from the close of November 30, as part of its November index review. It will publish the final list of affected companies on November 11. The decision follows a review MSCI began a year ago, when it proposed excluding digital asset treasury companies on the grounds that they resemble investment funds, which are already barred from its indexes. MSCI deferred that plan in January and opened a broader review on all non-operating companies.

MSCI defines non-operating companies as investment funds and business development companies, and other companies whose finances make them look like one. Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet are on MSCI's list of potential deletions. SharpLink and several other crypto treasury companies are on a watchlist for possible removal. The changes are aimed at expanding MSCI’s exclusions for passive investment vehicles, with companies required to meet financial tests on their operating assets to remain eligible. Index inclusion matters to companies such as Strategy because passive funds and other investors tracking benchmarks are required to hold their shares.  Strategy did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside business hours. The company warned last year that an exclusion would result in $2.8 billion of its stock being liquidated and would "chill" the industry. Strategy, which pioneered the model of raising money through stock and debt sales to buy bitcoin, had a market value of about $64.3 billion at Thursday’s close. Its shares were little changed in 2026.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Indian IT firm LTM beats second-quarter revenue view
item.description: Indian IT services firm LTM , formerly known as LTIMindtree, beat second-quarter revenue estimates on Friday as its consumer and tech segments performed strongly, but missed profit forecasts.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian IT services firm LTM , formerly known as LTIMindtree, beat second-quarter revenue estimates on Friday as its consumer and tech segments performed strongly, but missed profit forecasts. Consolidated revenue rose 13.6% year-on-year to 118.08 billion rupees ($1.24 billion) in the quarter ended September 30. Data compiled by LSEG showed that analysts, on average, expected 117.79 billion rupees. AI is disrupting India's $315-billion software services sector by undermining its billable hour business model, but is also creating new demand as clients buy services built on the technology. Companies are ramping up investments to capture this emerging demand and cushion the hit to their core business. LTM's revenue after stripping out currency fluctuations grew 5.1% in the second quarter. However, revenue from its consumer and tech segments outstripped that, growing 8.6% and 7%, respectively, on the same basis. Revenue from LTM's AI-native business grew 47% year-on-year, CEO Venu Lambu said in a statement, though he did not disclose the amount. In July, when the company first announced the metric, it said it derives $150 million in revenue on a quarterly run-rate basis across three AI-native businesses. Consolidated profit fell about 0.2% to 13.98 billion rupees ($147.22 million). Analysts had expected profit of 15.20 billion rupees. Deal wins for the quarter stood at $1.26 billion, down from $1.68 billion in the preceding quarter and $1.59 billion in the year-ago period. Larger rivals Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) , HCLTech (HCLT.NS) and Wipro (WIPR.NS) suggest demand has remained broadly resilient despite growing concerns over AI-led disruption, but have not flagged signs of significant improvement. Shares of LTM closed 3.7% higher on Friday ahead of its results, broadly in line with a 3.9% surge in the Nifty IT index (.NIFTYIT) , which logged its steepest weekly gain in 18 years. ($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

item.title: トヨタ、30年までに全車種をＳＤＶに 年1000万台の新車に独自ソフト搭載
item.description: [東京 １６日 ロイター] - トヨタ自動車は、２０３０年までに世界で販売する全５０車種を「ソフトウエア定義車両（Ｓ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
トヨタ、30年までに全車種をＳＤＶに　年1000万台の新車に独自ソフト搭載 20:20 配信

トヨタ自動車の「ＲＡＶ４」。２０２５年５月、東京で撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Manami Yamada）

[東京 １６日 ロイター] - トヨタ自動車は、２０３０年までに世界で販売する全５０車種を「ソフトウエア定義車両（ＳＤＶ）」にする。独自のソフトウェアプラットフォーム（基盤）「Ａｒｅｎｅ（アリーン）」を新車に順次搭載する。ＳＤＶで先行する中国や米国の電気自動車（ＥＶ）メーカーを追撃し、年間１０００万台規模の新車販売に加え、売った後もソフトの更新などを通じて課金するビジネスモデルを強化する。

同社広報によると、中嶋裕樹副社長が先週、アリーンの導入計画をベルギーのブリュッセルで投資家に説明。３５年にはトヨタ車以外にも展開し、提携先など他社の車両にアリーンを供給する考えも明らかにしたという。

トヨタは２５年に発売したスポーツ多目的車（ＳＵＶ）「ＲＡＶ４」で初めてアリーンを導入し、今後販売する新車に順次展開する方針を示唆していた。

ＳＤＶは、スマートフォンのように購入後も無線通信を通じてソフトを更新し、先進運転支援技術やエンタテイメントなど車の性能や機能を向上させる車で、米テスラや中国勢が先行している。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：サウジを揺さぶるフーシ派、攻撃力向上の背景は アングル：米国の「軽油ショック」、消費者の身の回りで着実に進行 コラム：トヨタ自動車、ＨＶ技術活用で再び成長軌道へ 焦点：トヨタの中国合弁2社に再編機運、市場縮小と競争激化で転換点 焦点：トヨタ社長、3年でなぜ交代　インフレが変えた時代の潮流 最終更新: 10/16(金) 20:20 ロイター

item.title: AI jitters, Trump's fading oil clout and China shock 2.0: The financial week in five charts
item.description: Every Friday, Reuters Open Interest distills the financial week into five key charts, spotlighting the major trends, surprises and overlooked moves that defined the past five days.
item.dc:creator: Anna Szymanski
item.content:encoded: Every Friday, Reuters Open Interest (ROI) distills the financial week into five key charts, spotlighting the major trends, surprises and overlooked moves that defined the past five days. AI DOMINANCE JAMIE MCGEEVER, ROI Markets Columnist: What goes up must ... keep going up? That has largely been the case for AI-related stocks since OpenAI launched ChatGPT nearly four years ago. JPMorgan Private Bank's Michael Cembalest reckons AI-related stocks have accounted for 75% of S&P 500 returns, 80% of earnings growth and 90% of capital-spending growth since ChatGPT's November 2022 launch. But the stock-market boom is [USN:L6N45Y0TW TEXT:"not necessarily translating"] into an equally powerful economic one for the US. And concerns are mounting over the scale of AI investment, how it is funded and whether it will ultimately deliver adequate returns. Perhaps what goes up must come down. Eventually. 2. DEBT STRAIN ANNA SZYMANSKI, ROI Editor-in-Charge: The [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"US Consumer Price Index"] rose 0.6% last month, faster than the 0.4% increase in August, bringing the 12-month rate to 3.7%, largely due to a 9.1% rise in gasoline prices. More worrying for markets, however, was the core inflation reading, which strips out food and energy. It jumped 0.3% in September, slightly above economists' consensus forecast, driven by notable increases in housing costs and airline fares. This heightened concerns that US interest rates will stay higher for longer as the Federal Reserve seeks to return inflation to its 2% target. That, in turn, caused investors to flee — or hedge — some of the [USN:L4N46111C TEXT:"more heavily indebted AI companies"], which may struggle to generate enough cash to service higher debt costs. CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , the AI-focused cloud-computing firm, was among the biggest losers on Thursday. Its 5-year credit default swap surged past 1,100 basis points at one point, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence, while the yield on the company's 2031 bond rose to as high as 16% before retreating. 3. DIMINISHING POWER RON BOUSSO, ROI Energy Columnist: US President Donald Trump's trademark ability to [USN:L6N45Y0SD TEXT:"talk down oil markets"] with a few words is fading as the Iran war drags on, leaving global energy prices far more exposed to escalation. The market's muted reaction to Trump's diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin is the latest example. This reflects a deeper problem. The loss of around 2 million barrels per day of refining capacity in Russia and the Middle East, and the sharp drawdown in global oil inventories since the start of the Iran war, have left energy markets in a precarious position that cannot be fixed through rhetoric or relatively small supply additions. 4. EXPORT BLITZ MIKE DOLAN, ROI Finance & Markets Columnist: China's trade surplus widened more than expected in September as [USN:AZN4TOTAU TEXT:"exports surged"], stoking anxiety in Europe and elsewhere about a "China shock 2.0" as more of the country's goods flow into overseas markets. Strong demand for semiconductors and green-tech products has kept China's factories humming. Exports jumped 36% from a year earlier — the fastest pace since February — up from 25% in August and well above forecasts for 26% growth. Import growth also beat expectations, but the trade surplus still reached $938 billion in the first nine months. It is now on track to top $1 trillion a month earlier than last year, adding to [USN:L6N45Y0XV TEXT:"pressure on Europe"] to push for a stronger yuan and fairer competition. 5. ASIAN EDGE GAVIN MAGUIRE, ROI Global Energy Transition Columnist: Oil supplies are recovering faster than fuel output in the Middle East, where several regional refineries remain offline after sustaining damage during the conflict with Iran. That bodes well for refiners in Asia, home to more refining capacity than any other region. The massive coastal complexes in India, China, South Korea and Singapore were built to receive crude oil in bulk and convert it into gasoline, diesel and jet fuel for global markets. If Middle Eastern crude exports continue to rise, [USN:L1N45S14J TEXT:"Asian refiners appear well positioned"] to capture much of the value created by turning those barrels into the fuels that power the global economy. Opinions expressed are those of the authors. They do not reflect the views of Reuters News, which, under the Trust Principles , is committed to integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.

item.title: Mercados emergentes recuperan terreno tras cuatro jornadas de pérdidas por dudas sobre inversión en IA
item.description: El índice de referencia de renta variable de mercados emergentes de MSCI subió un 0,8%, con los fabricantes de chips Samsung Electronics Co. y SK Hynix entre los principales impulsores del avance.
item.dc:creator: Peter Laca, Marcus Wong
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Las acciones de los mercados emergentes subieron a medida que los inversores volvieron a apostar por las acciones tecnológicas de Corea del Sur, mientras que la disminución de las expectativas sobre una inminente alza de tasas de interés en Estados Unidos contribuyó a impulsar las monedas de los países en desarrollo. El índice de referencia de renta variable de mercados emergentes de MSCI subió un 0,8%, con los fabricantes de chips Samsung Electronics Co. y SK Hynix entre los principales impulsores del avance. El índice aún se encamina a su peor caída semanal desde principios de marzo, tras cuatro sesiones negativas marcadas por la preocupación sobre la sostenibilidad de las inversiones en inteligencia artificial. Ver más: Dólar registra su mayor caída en más de un mes por temores sobre la inversión en IA “Lo que vimos esta semana fue un efecto contagioso generalizado y una reacción instintiva ante el temor a cómo podría evolucionar la deuda en el ámbito de la IA”, declaró Sree Kochugovindan, economista investigadora sénior de Aberdeen Investments, en Bloomberg TV. Es importante analizar “los matices entre quiénes se guían por el efectivo y quiénes por la deuda, y creo que esto empezará a hacerse evidente”, añadió. Aunque las declaraciones del presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, el viernes no modificaron las previsiones del mercado sobre tres aumentos más de las tasas de interés en los próximos 12 meses, la ausencia de un tono más agresivo frenó aún más las expectativas de un alza a finales de este mes. El dólar cayó por segundo día consecutivo, su primera caída seguida en más de un mes. El índice Kospi de Corea del Sur rompió una racha de siete días de pérdidas, y las entradas de capital extranjero contribuyeron a que el won se apreciara hasta un 1% frente al dólar. Tanto el florín húngaro como el rand sudafricano se apreciaron alrededor de un 0,5%, mientras que el índice MSCI de divisas de mercados emergentes subió un 0,3%. En contraste con el clima general positivo del mercado, los activos indonesios se desplomaron después de que MSCI Inc. anunciara que el país ya no reúne los requisitos para ser considerado un mercado emergente. El índice bursátil de referencia de Yakarta registró su mayor caída en casi tres décadas, la rupia se depreció hasta un 0,7% y los bonos en dólares del país fueron los que peor se comportaron. Ver más: Bitcoin cae por debajo de US$80.000 por primera vez en casi un mes: las razones MSCI indicó que está llevando a cabo consultas sobre una propuesta para reclasificar a Indonesia como mercado independiente, alegando que una rebaja a la categoría de mercado fronterizo no reflejaría adecuadamente la gravedad de los problemas del mercado del país. Si bien la reclasificación propuesta puede percibirse como “perjudicial para los activos indonesios”, el impacto inmediato en los flujos podría ser limitado, afirmó Christopher Wong, estratega de Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp. “Lo más importante es cómo esto podría afectar la confianza de los inversores”. MSCI también está intensificando el escrutinio del mercado bursátil turco, congelando algunos cambios en los índices y advirtiendo que su estatus de mercado emergente podría verse comprometido. El índice Borsa Istanbul 100 cayó hasta un 3,4% el viernes, extendiendo su descenso a cerca del 11% en el último mes. Varios bonos soberanos libaneses en dólares se situaron entre los de mejor rendimiento el viernes, después de que el gobernador del banco central dijera que espera un avance en las conversaciones con el FMI antes de fin de año sobre la controvertida ley bancaria. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Morning Bid: Tipping Point
item.description: Hello Morning Bid readers!
item.dc:creator: Anna Szymanski
item.content:encoded: Hello Morning Bid readers! Are we reaching an inflection point? Whether it’s the AI boom , the escalation in the Middle East , or the relationship between the US and Ukraine , this week brought further signs that markets and geopolitics may be nearing a breaking point. A significant [USN:L1N45Z05C TEXT:"AI-related selloff"] hit global markets this week amid growing concerns that rising interest rates could create funding challenges as the web of circular financings in the AI ecosystem grows ever more complex. Markets were [USN:L1N46202B TEXT:"calmer early on Friday"], but investors remain wary that higher borrowing costs could end a party that has helped keep the global economy chugging along over the past year despite the headwinds from both trade wars and actual wars. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (.SOX) recorded seven straight daily declines through Thursday, while Asia’s tech-heavy indices – some of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI euphoria earlier this year – [USN:L6N46100A TEXT:"were hit hard this week"]. South Korea's KOSPI index (.KS11) dropped almost 8% on Thursday, though it rose over 3% on Friday. The pullback was amplified on Wednesday by a slightly hotter-than-anticipated US CPI print. The Consumer Price Index [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"rose 0.6% last month"], increasing 3.7% in the 12 months through September, largely thanks to higher gasoline prices. This was in line with economists' expectations, but the 0.3% monthly rise in core inflation – which strips out food and energy prices – was slightly above consensus projections. This spooked markets, briefly boosting bets for another Federal Reserve interest rate hike this month to roughly 50% – up from roughly 25% before the inflation release. While that has since receded, markets still appear worried that sticky inflation will force the Fed to remain hawkish, as investors shed the equity and debt of some of the more heavily indebted companies. Most notably, CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) shares dropped 15% on Wednesday, while the cloud computing company's bonds due 2032, issued just four months ago, [USN:L6N46113P TEXT:"fell into distressed territory"] as its credit default swap spreads briefly blew out beyond 1,000 basis points. The [USN:L1N45Z05I TEXT:"International Monetary Fund"] put a spotlight on AI risk at its meetings in Bangkok this week. Jason Wu, assistant director of the IMF's Global Markets Analysis Division, warned: "If there are questions about the monetization of AI, the equity investments will deplete in value, the debt may be difficult to service, and the revenue commitments in the future may not materialize." That's not a pretty picture. Earnings releases from the AI giants in the coming weeks may ease some investor concerns – but the bar is very high. Just look at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) (2330.TW) , the world's largest manufacturer of advanced chips. It [USN:L4N45Y1DX TEXT:"reported a 69% jump"] in third-quarter net profit on Thursday, beating market forecasts, while noting that demand for chips is still outstripping supply. Yet this didn't do much to stop the bleeding across global AI equities. This points to a worrying question: are Wall Street’s AI bets [USN:L6N45V0ZS TEXT:"simply too big to succeed"]? [USN:L4N45V0IT TEXT:"Analysts expect"] earnings for S&P 500 (.SPX) companies to rise more than 30% year-over-year for the third quarter, with two-thirds of that coming from tech and AI, according to LSEG. But Wall Street banks, the first major set of companies to report this season, had a bit of a rocky start. The results from the likes of JPMorgan (JPM.N) , Citigroup (C.N) , Goldman Sachs (GS.N) and Wells Fargo (WFC.N) were mixed , but overall they indicate that the dealmaking and trading bonanza that powered [USN:L6N43F12X TEXT:"record-high earnings in the first six months"] of the year may be slowing in the face of higher borrowing costs. At the heart of that rise in interest rates is, of course, this year's energy-driven inflation surge. On that front, Brent crude rose above $106 a barrel on Wednesday amid escalating attacks in the Middle East, though it pared some of those gains later in the week. Yemen's Iran-aligned [USN:L6N460162 TEXT:"Houthis stepped up their attacks"] on Saudi Arabia throughout the week. The group hit oil giant Saudi Aramco's <2222.SE[USN:L6N4600O5 TEXT:"headquarters"] as well as [USN:S8N44Y00K TEXT:"Riyadh's international airport"]. The attacks came as the kingdom hosted a [USN:L8N45W01K TEXT:"major energy and investment conference"]. Iran also said it was deploying [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"new tactics to target ships"] transiting the Strait of Hormuz as Tehran seeks to keep upward pressure on oil prices ahead of the US November 3 midterm elections . A container ship and a dry bulk carrier both [USN:L8N46019A TEXT:"sank near Hormuz"] within 24 hours of each other after being struck by projectiles in separate incidents, according to maritime officials. Meanwhile, fuel prices remain sky-high, most notably diesel. While US President Donald Trump [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"announced a diesel deal"] with Russian President Vladimir Putin last Friday to enable Russia to resume some diesel exports and [USN:L8N45X02N TEXT:"claimed"] on Sunday that an energy ceasefire between the warring parties was in place, the impact on energy prices was modest. The volumes cited in the diesel agreement were very small and even though Kyiv initially agreed to suspend strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, the tenuous “ceasefire” arrangement had [USN:FWN4610DW TEXT:"unravelled by Thursday"]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy cited [USN:S8N44302A TEXT:"US "betrayal,""] as Ukrainian officials complained that they had not received any US early-warning alerts about incoming Russian ballistic missiles for multiple days. They also said the military version of Elon Musk's [USN:L1N4600Y1 TEXT:"Starlink satellite communications service"] had been slowed across the country, hampering their military activities. While the outlook for both the Middle East and Russia/Ukraine conflicts is murky — to say the least — one thing is becoming clear. Something in the mindset of energy traders is shifting. For many months, Trump was able to talk down oil markets with a few words, but energy price moves in recent weeks suggest that his [USN:L6N45Y0SD TEXT:"trademark ability is fading"]. Looking ahead to next week, geopolitics and earnings will likely vie for investor attention, as Meta (META.O) , Tesla (TSLA.O) and IBM (IBM.N) are all set to report. Before you head off, take a look at some questions ROI columnists have recently been exploring: Why aren’t Middle East LNG flows [USN:L6N45V0SD TEXT:"recovering as fast as crude?"] What’s left of the US economy [USN:L6N46015W TEXT:"when you strip away AI?"] Why aren’t surging yields [USN:L1N45U0R6 TEXT:"spooking corporate borrowers?"] Can the US maintain its [USN:L8N45V0YV TEXT:"strategic copper reserve?"] Why is yuan devaluation good news and [USN:L6N45Y0XV TEXT:"bad news for Europe?"] Might governments actually be [USN:L6N45Z13S TEXT:"rooting for AI to stumble?"] How has the aluminium market remained [USN:L8N45Y19S TEXT:"immune from the Iran war?"] Why might the road to an all-electric car fleet be [USN:L1N45Y0RF TEXT:"bumpier than expected?"] Could Asian oil refineries be among the [USN:L1N45S14J TEXT:"biggest winners of the Iran war?"] Why might AI be [USN:L6N45Y0TW TEXT:"weighing down US GDP?"] What’s the dirty secret behind [USN:L1N45N14U TEXT:"Europe’s battery boom?"] I'd love to hear from you, so please reach out to me at anna.szymanski@thomsonreuters.com . Want to receive the Morning Bid in your inbox every weekday morning? Sign up for the newsletter here . You can find ROI on the Reuters website , and you can follow us on LinkedIn and X .
